**Steven Williams** (born January 7, 1949) is an American actor in films and television. He is known for his roles as Captain Adam Fuller on _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street "21 Jump Street")_, NYPD Detective [Lt. Jefferson Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#Recurring "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)") on _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_, Det. August Brooks on _[L.A. Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A.\_Heat\_(TV\_series) "L.A. Heat (TV series)")_, [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_(The_X-Files) "X (The X-Files)") on _[The X-Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X-Files "The X-Files")_, Russell "Linc" Lincoln in _[Linc's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linc's "Linc's")_, and [Rufus Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Supernatural_characters#Rufus_Turner "List of Supernatural characters") in _[Supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural\_(American\_TV\_series) "Supernatural (American TV series)")_.

Throughout his career, Williams has appeared in numerous films, including _[The Blues Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blues\_Brothers\_(film) "The Blues Brothers (film)")_ (1980), _[Twilight Zone: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_Zone:\_The\_Movie "Twilight Zone: The Movie")_ (1983), _[Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason\_Goes\_to\_Hell:\_The\_Final\_Friday "Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday")_ (1993), _[22 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/22\_Jump\_Street "22 Jump Street")_ (2014), _[It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_(2017\_film) "It (2017 film)")_ (2017), and _[Birds of Prey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds\_of\_Prey\_(2020\_film) "Birds of Prey (2020 film)")_ (2020).

He has been nominated for a [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award") and one [NAACP Image Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP_Image_Award "NAACP Image Award").He starred in Family Business on BET +.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steven_Williams&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Williams was born in [Memphis, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee"), and was predominantly reared in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"). His parents were divorced, and he was raised at separate times by his father in [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan"), his mother in Chicago and by his maternal grandparents in [Millington, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millington,_Tennessee "Millington, Tennessee").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) In Chicago, he attended [Wendell Phillips High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendell_Phillips_High_School "Wendell Phillips High School"). After graduating, he matriculated at the [General Motors Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors_Institute "General Motors Institute"), an automaker's engineering school.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-YTD-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-3) Williams later worked as a postal carrier, salesman, and model.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-5)

He was drafted into the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army"), serving in the 2nd Armored Division, stationed in [Gelnhausen, Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelnhausen "Gelnhausen") and became Divisional Champion with the United States Army Boxing Team, Middleweight Division.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) Upon receiving an Honorable Discharge from the United States Army, Williams worked for the [United States Postal Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Postal_Service "United States Postal Service") as a mailman.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-YTD-1) After delivering the mail in subzero temperatures, he went to work in Chicago's garment district as an apparel salesman.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-YTD-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steven_Williams&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Williams made his acting debut in the 1975 film _[Cooley High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooley\_High "Cooley High")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) He appeared in musical comedy _[The Blues Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blues\_Brothers\_(film) "The Blues Brothers (film)")_ (1980) as Trooper Mount,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) and played Lt. Jefferson Burnett on the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") drama series _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_ in 1985.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) He portrayed renegade Capt. David Nester in the 1985 film _[Missing in Action 2: The Beginning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missing\_in\_Action\_2:\_The\_Beginning "Missing in Action 2: The Beginning")_,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-6)

He landed the role of Captain Adam Fuller,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-7) a senior police officer supervising younger cops,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) on [Fox Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Network "Fox Network")'s TV series _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street "21 Jump Street")_ in 1987.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-werner-8) Williams replaced [Frederic Forrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederic_Forrest "Frederic Forrest"), who played a similar character, early in the series.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) He continued playing the character until the series ended in 1991. While acting in the series, Williams played Lieutenant Gallagher in _[Under the Gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under\_the\_Gun\_(1988\_film) "Under the Gun (1988 film)")_ (1988), which featured [Vanessa Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Williams "Vanessa Williams") in the cast.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-9)

Following his stint on _21 Jump Street_, Williams portrayed the title character in _[The 100 Lives of Black Jack Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_100\_Lives\_of\_Black\_Jack\_Savage "The 100 Lives of Black Jack Savage")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-10) He played the role of Det. August Brooks on the [TNT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turner_Network_Television "Turner Network Television") series _[L.A. Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A.\_Heat\_(TV\_series) "L.A. Heat (TV series)")_ in 1996. He recurred as [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_(The_X-Files) "X (The X-Files)") on the [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") hit [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction") series _[The X-Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X-Files "The X-Files")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-11) He earned a [Screen Actors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild "Screen Actors Guild") nomination for [Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series") in 1997 for his work as X.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-12)

Williams appeared as main character Russell "Linc" Lincoln, a bartender,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-13) in comedy _[Linc's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linc's "Linc's")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-14) In 2000, he received an [NAACP Image Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP_Image_Award "NAACP Image Award") nomination, in the category of [Outstanding Actor in a Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP_Image_Award_for_Outstanding_Actor_in_a_Comedy_Series "NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Actor in a Comedy Series").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-15) Concurrently, Williams portrayed Isaac in short-lived [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Paramount_Network "United Paramount Network") series _[Legacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legacy\_(1998\_TV\_series) "Legacy (1998 TV series)")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-16)

He portrayed [Rufus Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Supernatural_characters#Rufus_Turner "List of Supernatural characters") in fantasy series _[Supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural\_(American\_TV\_series) "Supernatural (American TV series)")_ (2008−16),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-17) and was Quentin in drama _[The Chi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chi "The Chi")_ (2018−present).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-18) Williams' work on the latter has been well received, with reviewers finding him "strong"[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-19) and "powerful"[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-20) as Quentin. Williams garnered several recurring roles in the 2010s and 2020s, including attorney Stephen Carlisle in _[Ambitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambitions\_(TV\_series) "Ambitions (TV series)")_ (2019)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-21) and teacher Joe Ridgeway in _[Locke & Key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locke\_&\_Key\_(TV\_series) "Locke & Key (TV series)")_ (2020),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-22) both dramas.

Williams has appeared extensively in guest roles on television. He portrayed an Army friend of the protagonist in _[MacGyver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacGyver\_(1985\_TV\_series) "MacGyver (1985 TV series)")_,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-23) and was [Robin Dumars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangin'_with_Mr._Cooper#Cast "Hangin' with Mr. Cooper")' father on _[Hangin' with Mr. Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangin'\_with\_Mr.\_Cooper "Hangin' with Mr. Cooper")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-24) Other guest appearances include _[The Dukes of Hazzard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dukes\_of\_Hazzard "The Dukes of Hazzard")_, _[The A-Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A-Team "The A-Team")_, _[Booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booker\_(TV\_series) "Booker (TV series)")_, _[Stargate SG-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate\_SG-1 "Stargate SG-1")_, _[Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin\_(TV\_series) "Martin (TV series)")_, _[Veronica Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica\_Mars "Veronica Mars")_, _[The Bernie Mac Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bernie\_Mac\_Show "The Bernie Mac Show")_, _[Criminal Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal\_Minds "Criminal Minds")_ and _[iZombie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IZombie\_(TV\_series) "IZombie (TV series)")_.

Other film roles include a bar patron in _[Twilight Zone: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_Zone:\_The\_Movie "Twilight Zone: The Movie")_ (1983),[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-25)[bounty hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounty_hunter "Bounty hunter") Creighton Duke in [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason\_Goes\_to\_Hell:\_The\_Final\_Friday "Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday")_ (1993)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-26) and Carlos in _[Adventures of Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventures\_of\_Power "Adventures of Power")_ (2009).[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-27) In TV movies, Williams was a Panamanian boat captain named Mo in _[Dreams of Gold: The Mel Fisher Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreams\_of\_Gold:\_The\_Mel\_Fisher\_Story "Dreams of Gold: The Mel Fisher Story")_ (1986)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-28) and portrayed pitcher [Satchel Paige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satchel_Paige "Satchel Paige") in _[The Court-Martial of Jackie Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Court-Martial\_of\_Jackie\_Robinson "The Court-Martial of Jackie Robinson")_ (1990).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-29)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steven_Williams&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

He was previously married to talent agent Ann Geddes.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-werner-8) He has two daughters and six grandchildren.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) His eldest granddaughter is an artist based in Chicago and Los Angeles.

**Steven Williams** (born January 7, 1949) is an American actor in films and television. He is known for his roles as Captain Adam Fuller on _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street "21 Jump Street")_, NYPD Detective [Lt. Jefferson Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#Recurring "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)") on _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_, Det. August Brooks on _[L.A. Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A.\_Heat\_(TV\_series) "L.A. Heat (TV series)")_, [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_(The_X-Files) "X (The X-Files)") on _[The X-Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X-Files "The X-Files")_, Russell "Linc" Lincoln in _[Linc's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linc's "Linc's")_, and [Rufus Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Supernatural_characters#Rufus_Turner "List of Supernatural characters") in _[Supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural\_(American\_TV\_series) "Supernatural (American TV series)")_.

Throughout his career, Williams has appeared in numerous films, including _[The Blues Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blues\_Brothers\_(film) "The Blues Brothers (film)")_ (1980), _[Twilight Zone: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_Zone:\_The\_Movie "Twilight Zone: The Movie")_ (1983), _[Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason\_Goes\_to\_Hell:\_The\_Final\_Friday "Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday")_ (1993), _[22 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/22\_Jump\_Street "22 Jump Street")_ (2014), _[It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_(2017\_film) "It (2017 film)")_ (2017), and _[Birds of Prey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds\_of\_Prey\_(2020\_film) "Birds of Prey (2020 film)")_ (2020).

He has been nominated for a [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award") and one [NAACP Image Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP_Image_Award "NAACP Image Award").He starred in Family Business on BET +.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steven_Williams&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Williams was born in [Memphis, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee"), and was predominantly reared in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"). His parents were divorced, and he was raised at separate times by his father in [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan"), his mother in Chicago and by his maternal grandparents in [Millington, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millington,_Tennessee "Millington, Tennessee").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) In Chicago, he attended [Wendell Phillips High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendell_Phillips_High_School "Wendell Phillips High School"). After graduating, he matriculated at the [General Motors Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors_Institute "General Motors Institute"), an automaker's engineering school.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-YTD-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-3) Williams later worked as a postal carrier, salesman, and model.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-5)

He was drafted into the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army"), serving in the 2nd Armored Division, stationed in [Gelnhausen, Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelnhausen "Gelnhausen") and became Divisional Champion with the United States Army Boxing Team, Middleweight Division.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) Upon receiving an Honorable Discharge from the United States Army, Williams worked for the [United States Postal Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Postal_Service "United States Postal Service") as a mailman.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-YTD-1) After delivering the mail in subzero temperatures, he went to work in Chicago's garment district as an apparel salesman.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-YTD-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steven_Williams&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Williams made his acting debut in the 1975 film _[Cooley High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooley\_High "Cooley High")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) He appeared in musical comedy _[The Blues Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blues\_Brothers\_(film) "The Blues Brothers (film)")_ (1980) as Trooper Mount,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) and played Lt. Jefferson Burnett on the [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") drama series _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_ in 1985.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) He portrayed renegade Capt. David Nester in the 1985 film _[Missing in Action 2: The Beginning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missing\_in\_Action\_2:\_The\_Beginning "Missing in Action 2: The Beginning")_,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-6)

He landed the role of Captain Adam Fuller,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-7) a senior police officer supervising younger cops,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) on [Fox Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Network "Fox Network")'s TV series _[21 Jump Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_Jump\_Street "21 Jump Street")_ in 1987.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-werner-8) Williams replaced [Frederic Forrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederic_Forrest "Frederic Forrest"), who played a similar character, early in the series.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) He continued playing the character until the series ended in 1991. While acting in the series, Williams played Lieutenant Gallagher in _[Under the Gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under\_the\_Gun\_(1988\_film) "Under the Gun (1988 film)")_ (1988), which featured [Vanessa Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Williams "Vanessa Williams") in the cast.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-9)

Following his stint on _21 Jump Street_, Williams portrayed the title character in _[The 100 Lives of Black Jack Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_100\_Lives\_of\_Black\_Jack\_Savage "The 100 Lives of Black Jack Savage")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-10) He played the role of Det. August Brooks on the [TNT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turner_Network_Television "Turner Network Television") series _[L.A. Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A.\_Heat\_(TV\_series) "L.A. Heat (TV series)")_ in 1996. He recurred as [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_(The_X-Files) "X (The X-Files)") on the [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") hit [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction") series _[The X-Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_X-Files "The X-Files")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-11) He earned a [Screen Actors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild "Screen Actors Guild") nomination for [Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_an_Ensemble_in_a_Drama_Series "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series") in 1997 for his work as X.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-12)

Williams appeared as main character Russell "Linc" Lincoln, a bartender,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-13) in comedy _[Linc's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linc's "Linc's")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-14) In 2000, he received an [NAACP Image Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP_Image_Award "NAACP Image Award") nomination, in the category of [Outstanding Actor in a Comedy Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP_Image_Award_for_Outstanding_Actor_in_a_Comedy_Series "NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Actor in a Comedy Series").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-15) Concurrently, Williams portrayed Isaac in short-lived [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Paramount_Network "United Paramount Network") series _[Legacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legacy\_(1998\_TV\_series) "Legacy (1998 TV series)")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-16)

He portrayed [Rufus Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Supernatural_characters#Rufus_Turner "List of Supernatural characters") in fantasy series _[Supernatural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supernatural\_(American\_TV\_series) "Supernatural (American TV series)")_ (2008−16),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-17) and was Quentin in drama _[The Chi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chi "The Chi")_ (2018−present).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-18) Williams' work on the latter has been well received, with reviewers finding him "strong"[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-19) and "powerful"[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-20) as Quentin. Williams garnered several recurring roles in the 2010s and 2020s, including attorney Stephen Carlisle in _[Ambitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambitions\_(TV\_series) "Ambitions (TV series)")_ (2019)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-21) and teacher Joe Ridgeway in _[Locke & Key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locke\_&\_Key\_(TV\_series) "Locke & Key (TV series)")_ (2020),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-22) both dramas.

Williams has appeared extensively in guest roles on television. He portrayed an Army friend of the protagonist in _[MacGyver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacGyver\_(1985\_TV\_series) "MacGyver (1985 TV series)")_,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-23) and was [Robin Dumars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangin'_with_Mr._Cooper#Cast "Hangin' with Mr. Cooper")' father on _[Hangin' with Mr. Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangin'\_with\_Mr.\_Cooper "Hangin' with Mr. Cooper")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-24) Other guest appearances include _[The Dukes of Hazzard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dukes\_of\_Hazzard "The Dukes of Hazzard")_, _[The A-Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A-Team "The A-Team")_, _[Booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booker\_(TV\_series) "Booker (TV series)")_, _[Stargate SG-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate\_SG-1 "Stargate SG-1")_, _[Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin\_(TV\_series) "Martin (TV series)")_, _[Veronica Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronica\_Mars "Veronica Mars")_, _[The Bernie Mac Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bernie\_Mac\_Show "The Bernie Mac Show")_, _[Criminal Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal\_Minds "Criminal Minds")_ and _[iZombie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IZombie\_(TV\_series) "IZombie (TV series)")_.

Other film roles include a bar patron in _[Twilight Zone: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twilight\_Zone:\_The\_Movie "Twilight Zone: The Movie")_ (1983),[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-25)[bounty hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounty_hunter "Bounty hunter") Creighton Duke in [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason\_Goes\_to\_Hell:\_The\_Final\_Friday "Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday")_ (1993)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-26) and Carlos in _[Adventures of Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventures\_of\_Power "Adventures of Power")_ (2009).[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-27) In TV movies, Williams was a Panamanian boat captain named Mo in _[Dreams of Gold: The Mel Fisher Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreams\_of\_Gold:\_The\_Mel\_Fisher\_Story "Dreams of Gold: The Mel Fisher Story")_ (1986)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-28) and portrayed pitcher [Satchel Paige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satchel_Paige "Satchel Paige") in _[The Court-Martial of Jackie Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Court-Martial\_of\_Jackie\_Robinson "The Court-Martial of Jackie Robinson")_ (1990).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-29)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steven_Williams&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

He was previously married to talent agent Ann Geddes.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-werner-8) He has two daughters and six grandchildren.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Williams#cite_note-buck-2) His eldest granddaughter is an artist based in Chicago and Los Angeles.

## Filmography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steven_Williams&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Filmography")]

**Gerald Lee McRaney** (born August 19, 1947) is an American actor who has appeared in many popular movies and television shows. He is famous for his roles in TV series like _Simon & Simon_, _Major Dad_, and _NCIS: Los Angeles_.

McRaney has also been recognized for his powerful acting. He won a Primetime Emmy Award for his role as Dr. Nathan Katowski in the hit show _This Is Us_. Throughout his long career, he has played a wide variety of characters, from detectives and military officers to caring doctors.

## Early Life and First Jobs

Gerald McRaney was born in [Collins, Mississippi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Collins,_Mississippi "Collins, Mississippi"). His parents were Clyde and Edna McRaney, and he has [Scottish](https://kids.kiddle.co/Scottish_people "Scottish people") and [Choctaw](https://kids.kiddle.co/Choctaw "Choctaw") heritage. After graduating from high school, he went to the [University of Mississippi](https://kids.kiddle.co/University_of_Mississippi "University of Mississippi").

Before he became a successful actor, McRaney had a tough job working in the oil fields of [Louisiana](https://kids.kiddle.co/Louisiana "Louisiana"). This experience helped shape his hardworking attitude, which he later brought to his acting career.

## Acting Career

McRaney's acting career began in 1969. In his early years, he appeared in many popular TV shows. He had guest roles in shows like _[Gunsmoke](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gunsmoke "Gunsmoke")_, _[The Waltons](https://kids.kiddle.co/The\_Waltons "The Waltons")_, and _[The Incredible Hulk](https://kids.kiddle.co/The\_Incredible\_Hulk\_(1978\_TV\_series) "The Incredible Hulk (1978 TV series)")_. McRaney holds the distinction of being the last guest star to meet "Matt Dillon" in a gunfight on [Gunsmoke (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0047736/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) - in the episode, [Hard Labor (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0594133/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), first broadcast on February 24, 1975 (he lost). In fact, in the early portion of Gerald McRaney's career he almost always played the villain; but, since his first series, [Simon & Simon (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081930/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), hit it big, he's played mostly good guys. The character of passionate but irresponsible "Rick Simon" gave McRaney the opportunity to play a dramatic role with a comedic edge. A second hit series, [Major Dad (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0096643/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), showcased his talent for comedy. McRaney met and fell in love with fellow southerner [Delta Burke](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004785/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) when she guest-starred on [Simon & Simon (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081930/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He later appeared on her series, [Designing Women (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090418/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), as her ex-husband, although it is an unwritten rule that actors with current series don't do guest roles; they were married not long after.

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0574468/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

McRaney holds the distinction of being the last guest star to meet "Matt Dillon" in a gunfight on [Gunsmoke (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0047736/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) - in the episode, [Hard Labor (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0594133/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), first broadcast on February 24, 1975 (he lost). In fact, in the early portion of Gerald McRaney's career he almost always played the villain; but, since his first series, [Simon & Simon (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081930/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), hit it big, he's played mostly good guys. The character of passionate but irresponsible "Rick Simon" gave McRaney the opportunity to play a dramatic role with a comedic edge. A second hit series, [Major Dad (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0096643/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), showcased his talent for comedy. McRaney met and fell in love with fellow southerner [Delta Burke](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004785/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) when she guest-starred on [Simon & Simon (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081930/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He later appeared on her series, [Designing Women (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090418/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), as her ex-husband, although it is an unwritten rule that actors with current series don't do guest roles; they were married not long after.

Happy Birthday to the actor KENT McCORD.

First using his real name on television in 1962 in THE ADVENTURES OF OZZIE & HARRIET, he later adopted his stage name. He became a close friend of Rick Nelson and made 44 appearances on the program. He also landed small parts in five Elvis Presley films and (as Kent McWhirter) portrayed a motorcycle courier in MCHALE'S NAVY in the episode "Monkey Business 007".

McCord also appeared in the first episode of Raymond Burr's IRONSIDE series, titled "Message from Beyond".

In the first season of Jack Webb's DRAGNET 1967, he appeared three times. 

McCord's big break came in 1968 when he was given a lead role next to Martin Milner as rookie police officer James A. "Jim" Reed on ADAM-12, a police drama television series created by Jack Webb. The show ran on NBC from 1968 to 1975.

McCord was elected to the national board of directors of the Screen Actors Guild in 1972 and was on the board for 11 years. He was the first national vice president while on the National Board of Directors.

McCord appeared as a downed fighter ace on the 1970s series BAA BAA BLACK SHEEP. 

In 1980, he played Troy on the television series GALACTICA 1980. 

Two years later, Webb tabbed him for a new DRAGNET series he was ready to launch, with McCord to play the partner to Webb's Joe Friday.

In 1982, McCord played Mr. Unger on AIRPLANE II: THE SEQUEL.

In 1989, he co-starred on the crime drama UNSUB. 

He re-teamed with Martin Milner, his co-star in ADAM-12, in the cable TV-movie NASHVILLE BEAT (1990), originally shown on The Nashville Network. 

In 1990, McCord appeared in the film PREDATOR 2 as Captain Pilgrim. 

He played John Reynolds in RETURN OF THE LIVING DEAD 3 (1993).

From 1994 to 1995, McCord played the recurring role of Scott Keller on SEAQUEST DSV. 

He appeared in three episodes of JAG, and more recently, became a semi-regular guest star on FARSCAPE, where he played two versions (one human and one alien appearing in the physical form of the human) of the same character, Jack Crichton from 1999 to 2003, appearing in all four seasons. 

He played Deputy U.S. Marshal Jack Hendricks on the series Renegade.

**Michael Anthony Beach** (born October 30, 1963) is an American actor. He has appeared in the films _[Lean on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lean\_on\_Me\_(film) "Lean on Me (film)")_ (1989), _[One False Move](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_False\_Move "One False Move")_ (1992), _[True Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True\_Romance "True Romance")_ (1993), _[Short Cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short\_Cuts\_(film) "Short Cuts (film)")_ (1993), _[Waiting to Exhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waiting\_to\_Exhale "Waiting to Exhale")_ (1995), _[A Family Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Family\_Thing "A Family Thing")_ (1996), _[Soul Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Food\_(film) "Soul Food (film)")_ (1997), _[Aquaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquaman\_(film) "Aquaman (film)")_ (2018), _[If Beale Street Could Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If\_Beale\_Street\_Could\_Talk\_(film) "If Beale Street Could Talk (film)")_ (2018), and _[Saw X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saw\_X "Saw X")_ (2023). On television, he played Al Boulet on the NBC medical drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_ from 1995 to 1997. From 1999 to 2005, Beach was a regular cast member in another NBC drama series, _[Third Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third\_Watch "Third Watch")_, as Monte Parker, and as T.O. Cross in FX's _[Sons of Anarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons\_of\_Anarchy "Sons of Anarchy")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-2) Beach is widely known for portraying characters in multiple [crime dramas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_film "Crime film") including [S.W.A.T. (2017)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T._(2017_TV_series) "S.W.A.T. (2017 TV series)"), [Blue Bloods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Bloods "Blue Bloods") (2010) and [The Rookie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rookie "The Rookie") (2018).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-3)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Beach&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Beach was born in [Roxbury, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxbury,_Massachusetts "Roxbury, Massachusetts"), on October 30, 1963. He attended High School at the Noble and Greenough School in Dedham,MA. [[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-4)He graduated from [Juilliard School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juilliard_School "Juilliard School") with a degree for the [Bachelor of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Fine_Arts "Bachelor of Fine Arts"). His mother, [Barbara Gomes-Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Gomes-Beach "Barbara Gomes-Beach"), was of [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_people "Portuguese people") and [African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_diaspora "African diaspora") descent.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Beach&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Beach's big screen debut was in _[End of the Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End\_of\_the\_Line\_(1987\_film) "End of the Line (1987 film)")_ in 1987, and he went on to appear opposite [Morgan Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Freeman "Morgan Freeman") and [Beverly Todd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Todd "Beverly Todd") in _[Lean on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lean\_on\_Me\_(film) "Lean on Me (film)")_ (1989). Beach also co-starred in films including _[Internal Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal\_Affairs\_(film) "Internal Affairs (film)")_, _[Cadence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadence\_(film) "Cadence (film)")_ (both 1990), _[One False Move](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_False\_Move "One False Move")_ (1992) with [Cynda Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cynda_Williams "Cynda Williams"), _[Short Cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short\_Cuts "Short Cuts")_ and _[True Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True\_Romance "True Romance")_ (both 1993).

Beach's big break came in 1995, playing [Angela Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Bassett "Angela Bassett")'s unfaithful husband in the comedy-drama film _[Waiting to Exhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waiting\_to\_Exhale "Waiting to Exhale")_. In 1997, he played [Vanessa L. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_L._Williams "Vanessa L. Williams")'s unfaithful husband in the comedy-drama film _[Soul Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Food\_(film) "Soul Food (film)")_. On television, he played a recurring role as Al Boulet, the ex-husband of [physician assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physician_assistant "Physician assistant")[Jeanie Boulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanie_Boulet "Jeanie Boulet") ([Gloria Reuben](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Reuben "Gloria Reuben")) in the NBC medical drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_ from 1995 to 1997. From 1999 to 2005, Beach was a regular cast member in the NBC drama series _[Third Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third\_Watch "Third Watch")_, playing [FDNY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Fire_Department "New York City Fire Department") paramedic [Monte 'Doc' Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_'Doc'_Parker "Monte 'Doc' Parker").

Beach has had guest-starring roles on _[Law & Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law\_&\_Order "Law & Order")_, _[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law\_&\_Order:\_Special\_Victims\_Unit "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit")_, _[Brothers & Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers\_&\_Sisters\_(2006\_TV\_series) "Brothers & Sisters (2006 TV series)")_, _[Criminal Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal\_Minds "Criminal Minds")_, _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_, _[The Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Closer "The Closer")_, and _[The Blacklist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blacklist "The Blacklist")_. He was also a regular on the short-lived NBC series _[Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis\_(TV\_series) "Crisis (TV series)")_ in 2014, and had recurring roles on _[Stargate Atlantis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate\_Atlantis "Stargate Atlantis")_, _[Sons of Anarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons\_of\_Anarchy "Sons of Anarchy")_, _[The Client List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Client\_List\_(TV\_series) "The Client List (TV series)")_, _[The Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Game\_(2006\_TV\_series) "The Game (2006 TV series)")_, _[Secrets and Lies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secrets\_and\_Lies\_(American\_TV\_series) "Secrets and Lies (American TV series)")_, _[S.W.A.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T.\_(2017\_TV\_series) "S.W.A.T. (2017 TV series)")_ and _[The 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_100\_(TV\_series) "The 100 (TV series)")_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-5) Most recently he has had a guest-starring role in seasons 6 and 7 of _[Chicago P.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_P.D.\_(TV\_series) "Chicago P.D. (TV series)")_ as Darius Walker, a drug dealer and community philanthropist turned [confidential informant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confidential_informant "Confidential informant").

In December 2022, Beach was confirmed by _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline\_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ to have signed on to appear in _[Saw X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saw\_X "Saw X")_, the tenth installment of the _[Saw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saw\_(franchise) "Saw (franchise)")_ film series, for release in October 2023.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-Beach-6)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Beach&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Beach married Tracey Beach in 1990, and their marriage lasted until their divorce in 2006. The following year, he married Elisha Wilson.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-7)

**Michael Anthony Beach** (born October 30, 1963) is an American actor. He has appeared in the films _[Lean on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lean\_on\_Me\_(film) "Lean on Me (film)")_ (1989), _[One False Move](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_False\_Move "One False Move")_ (1992), _[True Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True\_Romance "True Romance")_ (1993), _[Short Cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short\_Cuts\_(film) "Short Cuts (film)")_ (1993), _[Waiting to Exhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waiting\_to\_Exhale "Waiting to Exhale")_ (1995), _[A Family Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Family\_Thing "A Family Thing")_ (1996), _[Soul Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Food\_(film) "Soul Food (film)")_ (1997), _[Aquaman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquaman\_(film) "Aquaman (film)")_ (2018), _[If Beale Street Could Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If\_Beale\_Street\_Could\_Talk\_(film) "If Beale Street Could Talk (film)")_ (2018), and _[Saw X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saw\_X "Saw X")_ (2023). On television, he played Al Boulet on the NBC medical drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_ from 1995 to 1997. From 1999 to 2005, Beach was a regular cast member in another NBC drama series, _[Third Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third\_Watch "Third Watch")_, as Monte Parker, and as T.O. Cross in FX's _[Sons of Anarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons\_of\_Anarchy "Sons of Anarchy")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-2) Beach is widely known for portraying characters in multiple [crime dramas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_film "Crime film") including [S.W.A.T. (2017)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T._(2017_TV_series) "S.W.A.T. (2017 TV series)"), [Blue Bloods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Bloods "Blue Bloods") (2010) and [The Rookie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rookie "The Rookie") (2018).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-3)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Beach&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Beach was born in [Roxbury, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxbury,_Massachusetts "Roxbury, Massachusetts"), on October 30, 1963. He attended High School at the Noble and Greenough School in Dedham,MA. [[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-4)He graduated from [Juilliard School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juilliard_School "Juilliard School") with a degree for the [Bachelor of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Fine_Arts "Bachelor of Fine Arts"). His mother, [Barbara Gomes-Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Gomes-Beach "Barbara Gomes-Beach"), was of [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_people "Portuguese people") and [African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_diaspora "African diaspora") descent.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Beach&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Beach's big screen debut was in _[End of the Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End\_of\_the\_Line\_(1987\_film) "End of the Line (1987 film)")_ in 1987, and he went on to appear opposite [Morgan Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Freeman "Morgan Freeman") and [Beverly Todd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Todd "Beverly Todd") in _[Lean on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lean\_on\_Me\_(film) "Lean on Me (film)")_ (1989). Beach also co-starred in films including _[Internal Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal\_Affairs\_(film) "Internal Affairs (film)")_, _[Cadence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadence\_(film) "Cadence (film)")_ (both 1990), _[One False Move](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_False\_Move "One False Move")_ (1992) with [Cynda Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cynda_Williams "Cynda Williams"), _[Short Cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short\_Cuts "Short Cuts")_ and _[True Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True\_Romance "True Romance")_ (both 1993).

Beach's big break came in 1995, playing [Angela Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Bassett "Angela Bassett")'s unfaithful husband in the comedy-drama film _[Waiting to Exhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waiting\_to\_Exhale "Waiting to Exhale")_. In 1997, he played [Vanessa L. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_L._Williams "Vanessa L. Williams")'s unfaithful husband in the comedy-drama film _[Soul Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Food\_(film) "Soul Food (film)")_. On television, he played a recurring role as Al Boulet, the ex-husband of [physician assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physician_assistant "Physician assistant")[Jeanie Boulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeanie_Boulet "Jeanie Boulet") ([Gloria Reuben](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Reuben "Gloria Reuben")) in the NBC medical drama _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_ from 1995 to 1997. From 1999 to 2005, Beach was a regular cast member in the NBC drama series _[Third Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third\_Watch "Third Watch")_, playing [FDNY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Fire_Department "New York City Fire Department") paramedic [Monte 'Doc' Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_'Doc'_Parker "Monte 'Doc' Parker").

Beach has had guest-starring roles on _[Law & Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law\_&\_Order "Law & Order")_, _[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law\_&\_Order:\_Special\_Victims\_Unit "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit")_, _[Brothers & Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers\_&\_Sisters\_(2006\_TV\_series) "Brothers & Sisters (2006 TV series)")_, _[Criminal Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal\_Minds "Criminal Minds")_, _[Grey's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grey's\_Anatomy "Grey's Anatomy")_, _[The Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Closer "The Closer")_, and _[The Blacklist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Blacklist "The Blacklist")_. He was also a regular on the short-lived NBC series _[Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis\_(TV\_series) "Crisis (TV series)")_ in 2014, and had recurring roles on _[Stargate Atlantis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate\_Atlantis "Stargate Atlantis")_, _[Sons of Anarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sons\_of\_Anarchy "Sons of Anarchy")_, _[The Client List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Client\_List\_(TV\_series) "The Client List (TV series)")_, _[The Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Game\_(2006\_TV\_series) "The Game (2006 TV series)")_, _[Secrets and Lies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secrets\_and\_Lies\_(American\_TV\_series) "Secrets and Lies (American TV series)")_, _[S.W.A.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T.\_(2017\_TV\_series) "S.W.A.T. (2017 TV series)")_ and _[The 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_100\_(TV\_series) "The 100 (TV series)")_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-5) Most recently he has had a guest-starring role in seasons 6 and 7 of _[Chicago P.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_P.D.\_(TV\_series) "Chicago P.D. (TV series)")_ as Darius Walker, a drug dealer and community philanthropist turned [confidential informant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confidential_informant "Confidential informant").

In December 2022, Beach was confirmed by _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline\_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ to have signed on to appear in _[Saw X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saw\_X "Saw X")_, the tenth installment of the _[Saw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saw\_(franchise) "Saw (franchise)")_ film series, for release in October 2023.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-Beach-6)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Beach&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Beach married Tracey Beach in 1990, and their marriage lasted until their divorce in 2006. The following year, he married Elisha Wilson.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Beach#cite_note-7)

In June 1967, Mariska and her brothers Zoltan and Mickey Jr. were in the back seat of a car when it was involved in the fatal accident which killed her mother. The children escaped with minor injuries. Her father remarried a stewardess named Ellen, and they raised the three children and gave them a normal childhood. Mariska majored in theater at UCLA. Her first motion picture feature was the cult favorite, Ghoulies (1984), where she gave a memorable performance as Donna. Unlike her mother Jayne, who had changed her name, her hair color, and did nude pictorials to become a star, Mariska took a very different approach on her journey to become a star. She rejected advice to change her name and appearance. And she refused to copy her mother's sexy image by turning down nude scenes in her next film Jocks (1986). She told casting directors that she was her own person when she held onto her dark locks and athletic figure, when they were expecting another blond, buxom Jayne Mansfield. She reaped the rewards from the hit TV show, after struggling and studying her craft for fifteen years. Best known for his starring role as Det. Sonny Crockett on the hugely successful TV series Miami Vice (1984), Don Johnson is one of the stars who really defined the 1980s. As James "Sonny" Crockett he went toe-to-toe with drug dealers, pimps, prostitutes, assassins, illegal arms-dealers and crooked cops on a weekly basis from 1984 to 1989, appearing in a grand total of 110 episodes. The show, which was executive-produced by four time Oscar-nominated director, producer and writer Michael Mann, paired Johnson with the equally cool Philip Michael Thomas as Det. Ricardo Tubbs and the calm and stoic presence of Edward James Olmos as Lt. Martin Castillo. It revolutionized television with its modern fashion, pop music, unique style and use of real locations. Johnson typically wore $1000 Armani, Versace and Hugo Boss suits over pastel cotton T-shirts, drove a Ferrari 365 GTS/4 Daytona (later a Ferrari Testarossa) and lived on an Endeavour 42-foot sailboat named "St. Vitus' Dance" with his pet alligator Elvis. He also had full use of an offshore powerboat. Still, "Miami Vice" had not only style but substance, and his portrayal of the Vietnam veteran turned vice detective turned Sonny Crockett into the world's favorite cop. For his work on "Miami Vice" Johnson won a Golden Globe for Best Performance by an Actor in a TV Series in 1986, and was nominated in the same category a year later. He also picked up an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series in 1985.

Johnson was born in Flat Creek, Missouri, the son Eva Lea "Nell" (Wilson), a beautician, and Wayne Fred Johnson, a farmer. As a kid, he wanted to become a professional bowler. Later, after a few brushes with the law at a young age, he discovered acting. After working on the stage for a while he ventured into films and television, but was not able to break into stardom despite, among other things, starring in the sci-fi cult classic A Boy and His Dog (1975).

Johnson starred in four failed TV pilots before landing his career-high role on "Miami Vice", which propelled him to superstardom. He directed four highly praised episodes of the show. He balanced his work on the series by appearing in a praised TV-movie adaption of the William Faulkner novel The Long Hot Summer (1985) and the feature Sweet Hearts Dance (1988) with Susan Sarandon. After the series ended he focused solely on his film career. Although movies like Dead Bang (1989), The Hot Spot (1990) and Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man (1991) did not fare well with the critics, quite a few of them have obtained a considerable cult following, with fans praising them as all being quality contributions to their genre. His film work has given Johnson the opportunity to work with legendary filmmakers like John Frankenheimer, Sidney Lumet and Dennis Hopper.

After working steadily, Johnson returned to TV in 1996 with the cop show Nash Bridges (1996). The show, which Johnson created and produced, did very well. It co-starred Cheech Marin and Jodi Lyn O'Keefe. Johnson played the title role, a captain in the San Francisco PD's Special Investigations Unit. He was again paired with a flashy vehicle, this time an electric-yellow 1971 Plymouth Barracuda convertible. After "Nash Bridges" went off the air Johnson kept a low profile, but continued to appear in films and on television. He starred in the failed WB courtroom drama Just Legal (2005), which was produced by Jerry Bruckheimer, and traveled to Europe to make the Norwegian screwball comedy Lange flate ballær II (2008) and the Italian films Bastardi (2008) and Torno a vivere da solo (2008). As a supporting actor, he's been seen in mainstream films such as Machete (2010), Django Unchained (2012) and Knives Out (2019).

Johnson had two pre-fame marriages that were annulled within a matter of days. In the early 1970s, he lived with rock groupie Pamela Des Barres. In 1972, Tippi Hedren, his co-star in The Harrad Experiment (1973), allowed him to date her daughter Melanie Griffith despite the fact she was only 14 and he was 22; the relationship culminated in a six-month marriage during 1976. From 1981 to 1985, he lived with actress Patti D'Arbanville and they had one son together. After short-lived liaisons with Cybill Shepherd, Barbra Streisand and a barely legal Uma Thurman, he remarried Griffith in 1989. The couple divorced again in 1996, after she left him for Antonio Banderas. Johnson was engaged to "Nash Bridges" co-star O'Keefe, but broke it off before they made it to the altar. Since 1999 he's been married to former debutante Kelley Phleger, with whom he has three children.

He was born Alfred Thomas Highmore in Camden Town, London, England, to Sue (Latimer), a talent agent, and Edward Thomas Highmore, an actor. Highmore has a younger brother, Albert "Bertie" Highmore. He attended Highgate School, and later earned a double-first degree in Spanish and Arabic from Cambridge University's Emmanuel College.  
  
In 1999, Highmore made his big screen debut in the comedy [Women Talking Dirty (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0180316/?ls), portraying [Helena Bonham Carter](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000307/?ls)'s son. His next prominent role was in the family drama [Two Brothers (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0338512/?ls). Highmore's breakout role came when he was cast in [Finding Neverland (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0308644/?ls), alongside [Johnny Depp](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000136/?ls) and [Kate Winslet](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000701/?ls). He was then cast in the title role of Charlie Bucket in [Tim Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000318/?ls)'s [Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0367594/?ls), and was reportedly recommended by co-star Johnny Depp. Roles in [A Good Year (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0401445/?ls) and [Arthur and the Invisibles (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0344854/?ls) soon followed, before he portrayed the title role in [August Rush (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0426931/?ls), opposite [Keri Russell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005392/?ls) and [Robin Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000245/?ls).  
  
In 2013, he began starring as the iconic Norman Bates in the drama thriller series [Bates Motel (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2188671/?ls), alongside [Vera Farmiga](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0267812/?ls) as his mother. Highmore received much acclaim for his performance throughout the series' run, and was nominated for multiple Saturn Awards and Critics' Choice Television Awards.  
  
2017- Stars in The Good Doctor as Shaun Murphy -a young autistic surgeon who has savant syndrome, relocates from a quiet country life to join the surgical unit at the prestigious San Jose St. Bonaventure Hospital. Shaun is alone in the world and unable to personally connect with those around him, but he finds his niche using his extraordinary medical skill and intuition to save lives and challenge the skepticism of his colleagues.

The choice set him apart from the hundreds of boys vying for the role. The director, Wayne Wang, loved the idea and even used it in the film. In 2006, Luke was cast in Walden Media's "How to Eat Fried Worms" as the main character of "Billy Forrester." Other credits include starring in the Disney Channel's original movies "Minutemen" and "Girl vs. Monster." Luke's other past motion picture credits include playing the role of autistic teen "Alan Wheddon" in "Dear John." As well as a vast collection of failed pilots, including Amazon's "Point of Honor", helmed by Carlton Cuse.  
  
Benward was born in Franklin, Tennessee, to [Kenda Benward](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1349770/?ls) (née Wilkerson), an actress/coach, and [Aaron Benward](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2485463/?ls), a singer/ songwriter. His grandfather, [Jeoffrey Benward](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm5954120/?ls), was a Contemporary Christian music singer. Part of an entertainment family, Luke got his acting bug by tagging along to auditions with his mother, actress, acting coach and CMT's first on-air personality, Kenda Benward. He got his musical heritage from his father, Aaron Benward, an award-winning producer, songwriter and recording artist. Luke is truly a triple threat. He studied dance with hip hop choreographer, Nick Bass (Britney Spears, Chris Brown, Christina Aguilera, and Michael Jackson) for four years. He also recorded his first five-song EP called Let Your Love Out in 2008 and supported that effort with a fall and spring 50 city tour.  
  
 Benward resides in Los Angeles, California .

George MacKay was born in 1992 in Hammersmith, London, England, to Kim Baker, a British costume designer, and Paul Christopher MacKay, an Australian stage/lighting manager, from Adelaide. One of his grandmothers is from Cork, Ireland.  
  
At the age of ten, George was scouted to audition for a role in the family feature [Peter Pan (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0316396/?ls). He quickly landed the part of Curly, one of the Lost Boys, and went on to have several minor roles on TV, including an episode of [Rose and Maloney (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0338655/?ls) and [Footprints in the Snow (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0452622/?ls). At thirteen, George landed the part of Riccio in the film adaptation of Cornelia Funke's best-selling children's novel [The Thief Lord (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0430674/?ls), starring [Aaron Taylor-Johnson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1093951/?ls) and was also cast in lead role for the BBC adaptation of Terry Pratchett's [Johnny and the Bomb (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0498319/?ls).  
  
George worked with [Tim Roth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000619/?ls), [Chiwetel Ejiofor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0252230/?ls) and [Sophie Okonedo](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0645683/?ls) for the HBO Movie [Tsunami: The Aftermath (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0758789/?ls) and later took a part in the Dickensian drama [The Old Curiosity Shop (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1023343/?ls). Soon after, George co-starred with [Daniel Craig](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0185819/?ls) and [Liev Schreiber](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000630/?ls) on [Defiance (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1034303/?ls). In 2009, George took on the role of Harry, in [The Boys Are Back (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0926380/?ls) alongside [Clive Owen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0654110/?ls), for which he received two award nominations. His career took another step forward with [Hunky Dory (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1727300/?ls).  
  
Since then, George featured in several shorts that have been popular on the festival circuit and played the part of Tommo Peaceful with counterpart [Jack O'Connell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1925239/?ls) in the adaptation of [Michael Morpurgo](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0606190/?ls)'s [Private Peaceful (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1667439/?ls).  
  
2013 was George's breakthrough year, and he was recognized for his parts as Aaron in [For Those in Peril (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2315628/?ls), Davy in the musical [Sunshine on Leith (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2481198/?ls), Jake Whittam in [Breakfast with Jonny Wilkinson (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3198544/?ls), and the dark horse Eddie in [How I Live Now (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1894476/?ls). George received several nominations for such features and later bought home a total of five awards.  
  
George had a stint in the West End in 2014 in The Cement Garden. He portrayed Joe in the well-received [Pride (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3169706/?ls) and [Duane Hopkins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1109502/?ls)' [Bypass (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2990816/?ls) premiered at the BFI London Film Festival in October. Both Captain Fantastic and [Sadie Jones](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1297779/?ls)' [The Outcast (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1585275/?ls) are in post-production and George will be returning to theatre for Eugene O'Neill's '"Ah,Wilderness!" this April.  
  
In 2016, George starred in the film [Captain Fantastic (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3553976/?ls), opposite [Viggo Mortensen](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001557/?ls), and the mini-series [11.22.63 (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2879552/?ls), with [James Franco](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0290556/?ls) and [Sarah Gadon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0300589/?ls). He rounded out the decade playing the starring role in Sam Mendes' [1917 (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8579674/?ls), a box office hit and highly critically acclaimed drama set during World War I, and shot to simulate a single take in real time.

In 2013, he began starring as the iconic Norman Bates in the drama thriller series [Bates Motel (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2188671/?ls), alongside [Vera Farmiga](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0267812/?ls) as his mother. Highmore received much acclaim for his performance throughout the series' run, and was nominated for multiple Saturn Awards and Critics' Choice Television Awards.  
  
2017- Stars in The Good Doctor as Shaun Murphy -a young autistic surgeon who has savant syndrome, relocates from a quiet country life to join the surgical unit at the prestigious San Jose St. Bonaventure Hospital. [![Image 17: James Stewart (May 20, 1908 – July 2, 1997) was an American actor and one of the most iconic figures of Hollywood's Golden Age. He was known for his warm and relatable personality, distinctive voice, and natural acting style. Over the course of his career, he appeared in more than 80 films, excelling in both comedic and dramatic roles. In 1935, Stewart signed a contract with MGM, marking the start of his film career. He gained widespread fame with Frank Capra's "Mr. Smith Goes to Washington" (1939) and "It's a Wonderful Life" (1946). In 1940, he won the Academy Award for Best Actor for his performance in "The Philadelphia Story." [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167086/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

Eric was born in Staten Island, New York, May 24. His father is an orthopedic surgeon and his mother is an artist. Eric is the eldest of three brothers. He graduated with a B.A. in communications from the University of Southern California in 1989. He married Keri Moyers in 1995 and they have two daughters, Katie and Ella.  
  
Eric Close is an actor, director, and writer. He has starred opposite [Tommy Flanagan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0281107/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in the Amazon film [Legal Action (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7656570/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as an attorney who must defend his brother-in-law on a murder charge. He can also be seen as Ltc. Jacobsen in the war drama [Indivisible (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6512428/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), based on the true story about a family's real-life events during the 2007 Iraq War.  
  
Close starred opposite [Connie Britton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0110168/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in the hit series [Nashville (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2281375/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), created by Oscar-winning writer [Callie Khouri](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451884/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) for the ABC network. Before this, Close starred for almost a decade in the critically acclaimed CBS series [Without a Trace (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0321021/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), nominated for a Golden Globe for best ensemble cast. Close then teamed up again with the network as the lead of their dramedy series [Chaos (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1591468/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), opposite [Tim Blake Nelson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0625789/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Close also starred as crafty lawyer Travis Tanner in the critically acclaimed USA series [Suits (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1632701/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). On the feature side, Close joined [Bradley Cooper](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0177896/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in [Clint Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000142/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s [American Sniper (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2179136/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) for Warner Bros., playing DIA Agent Snead.  
  
Past credits also include the series [The Magnificent Seven (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0129695/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Now and Again (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0212395/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Dark Skies (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115151/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [McKenna (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108853/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), while taking on a number of long-form features such as [American Me (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0103671/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Seven Deadly Sins (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1492152/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [NTSB: The Crash of Flight 323 (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285074/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Christmas Crime Story (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5813808/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Hercules and the Lost Kingdom (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110017/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Follow the Stars Home (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0284123/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [The Stranger Beside Me (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114559/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Long Island Fever (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0178710/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Without Consent (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0111733/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [Unanswered Prayers (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1733733/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which was produced by [Garth Brooks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004779/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Not to mention the Golden Globe-nominated miniseries [Taken (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0289830/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which was executive produced by [Steven Spielberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000229/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Behind the camera, Close is also an accomplished director. In addition to directing episodes of [Nashville (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2281375/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Without a Trace (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0321021/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), Eric finished directing and acting in his fourth feature for the Hallmark channel, which included the network's highest-rated Christmas film, [Christmas at Graceland (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8694374/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and Hallmark Hall of Fame's film [A Christmas Love Story (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt9747440/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), starring [Kristin Chenoweth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0155693/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Scott Wolf](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0937930/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and Close himself.

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167086/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

Eric was born in Staten Island, New York, May 24. His father is an orthopedic surgeon and his mother is an artist. Eric is the eldest of three brothers. He graduated with a B.A. in communications from the University of Southern California in 1989. He married Keri Moyers in 1995 and they have two daughters, Katie and Ella.  
  
Eric Close is an actor, director, and writer. He has starred opposite [Tommy Flanagan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0281107/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in the Amazon film [Legal Action (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7656570/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) as an attorney who must defend his brother-in-law on a murder charge. He can also be seen as Ltc. Jacobsen in the war drama [Indivisible (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6512428/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), based on the true story about a family's real-life events during the 2007 Iraq War.  
  
Close starred opposite [Connie Britton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0110168/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in the hit series [Nashville (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2281375/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), created by Oscar-winning writer [Callie Khouri](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451884/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) for the ABC network. Before this, Close starred for almost a decade in the critically acclaimed CBS series [Without a Trace (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0321021/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), nominated for a Golden Globe for best ensemble cast. Close then teamed up again with the network as the lead of their dramedy series [Chaos (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1591468/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), opposite [Tim Blake Nelson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0625789/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Close also starred as crafty lawyer Travis Tanner in the critically acclaimed USA series [Suits (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1632701/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). On the feature side, Close joined [Bradley Cooper](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0177896/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) in [Clint Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000142/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk)'s [American Sniper (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2179136/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) for Warner Bros., playing DIA Agent Snead.  
  
Past credits also include the series [The Magnificent Seven (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0129695/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Now and Again (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0212395/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Dark Skies (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0115151/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [McKenna (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0108853/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), while taking on a number of long-form features such as [American Me (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0103671/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Seven Deadly Sins (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1492152/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [NTSB: The Crash of Flight 323 (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285074/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Christmas Crime Story (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5813808/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Hercules and the Lost Kingdom (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0110017/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Follow the Stars Home (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0284123/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [The Stranger Beside Me (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114559/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Long Island Fever (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0178710/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Without Consent (1994)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0111733/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and [Unanswered Prayers (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1733733/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which was produced by [Garth Brooks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004779/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Not to mention the Golden Globe-nominated miniseries [Taken (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0289830/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which was executive produced by [Steven Spielberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000229/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Behind the camera, Close is also an accomplished director. In addition to directing episodes of [Nashville (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2281375/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Without a Trace (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0321021/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), Eric finished directing and acting in his fourth feature for the Hallmark channel, which included the network's highest-rated Christmas film, [Christmas at Graceland (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8694374/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and Hallmark Hall of Fame's film [A Christmas Love Story (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt9747440/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), starring [Kristin Chenoweth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0155693/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Scott Wolf](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0937930/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), and Close himself.
