**Samuel Pack Elliott** (born August 9, 1944) is an American actor. With a career spanning nearly six decades of [film and television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott_filmography "Sam Elliott filmography"), he is recognized for his deep [sonorous](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/sonorous "wiktionary:sonorous") voice. Elliott has received [various accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Sam_Elliott "List of awards and nominations received by Sam Elliott"), including a [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Awards "Screen Actors Guild Awards") and a [National Board of Review Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review"), in addition to nominations for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"), two [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") and two [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards").

Elliott began his career with minor roles on screen, making his film debut in the western _[The Way West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Way\_West\_(film) "The Way West (film)")_ (1967). After his first leading film role in the horror _[Frogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frogs\_(film) "Frogs (film)")_ (1972), Elliott gained wider attention with his [breakthrough role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") in the drama _[Lifeguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifeguard\_(film) "Lifeguard (film)")_ (1976). He achieved commercial success with his role in the biopic _[Mask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mask\_(1985\_film) "Mask (1985 film)")_ (1985) and received Golden Globe nominations for starring in [Louis L'Amour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_L'Amour "Louis L'Amour")'s adaptation of _[Conagher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conagher "Conagher")_ (1991). Elliott starred with Patrick Swayze in the movie _[Road House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_House\_(1989\_film) "Road House (1989 film)")_ (1989) and the miniseries _[Buffalo Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo\_Girls\_(miniseries) "Buffalo Girls (miniseries)")_ (1995), the latter of which also earned him his first [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Supporting_Actor_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie") nomination. Throughout the 1990s, he portrayed [John Buford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Buford "John Buford") in the historical drama _[Gettysburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gettysburg\_(1993\_film) "Gettysburg (1993 film)")_ (1993), [Virgil Earp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil_Earp "Virgil Earp") in the western _[Tombstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tombstone\_(film) "Tombstone (film)")_ (1993), [Sgt. Buckey O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckey_O'Neill "Buckey O'Neill") in the epic war miniseries _[Rough Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rough\_Riders\_(miniseries) "Rough Riders (miniseries)")_ (1997), and the Stranger in the crime comedy _[The Big Lebowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Lebowski "The Big Lebowski")_ (1998).

In ensuing decades, Elliott established himself as a [character actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_actor "Character actor"), with supporting roles in a number of films, such as the drama _[We Were Soldiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_Were\_Soldiers "We Were Soldiers")_ (2002) and [Marvel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Entertainment "Marvel Entertainment") superhero films _[Hulk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulk\_(film) "Hulk (film)")_ (2003) and _[Ghost Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Rider\_(2007\_film) "Ghost Rider (2007 film)")_ (2007). In the 2010s, he had guest starring roles in the [FX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_(TV_channel) "FX (TV channel)") neo-western series _[Justified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justified\_(TV\_series) "Justified (TV series)")_ (2015) and the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") comedy series _[Grace and Frankie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace\_and\_Frankie "Grace and Frankie")_ (2016) and subsequently starred in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") sitcom _[The Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ranch "The Ranch")_ (2016–2020). He went on to headline the comedy drama film _[The Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hero\_(2017\_film) "The Hero (2017 film)")_ (2017) and star opposite [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga") and [Bradley Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_Cooper "Bradley Cooper") in Cooper's [2018 adaptation of _A Star Is Born_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Star_Is_Born_(2018_film) "A Star Is Born (2018 film)"), for which he received critical acclaim and a nomination for the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor"). His role in the [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") western miniseries _[1883](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1883\_(TV\_series) "1883 (TV series)")_ (2021–2022) earned him further praise and a [SAG Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Male_Actor_in_a_Miniseries_or_Television_Movie "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Miniseries or Television Movie").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Samuel_Elliott_1962.jpg/250px-Samuel_Elliott_1962.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Samuel_Elliott_1962.jpg)

Elliott's high school yearbook photo

Samuel Pack Elliott was born August 9, 1944, at the [Sutter Memorial Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutter_Memorial_Hospital "Sutter Memorial Hospital") in [Sacramento, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento,_California "Sacramento, California"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-SElliottBorn-NYT-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-2) the son of Glynn Mamie (née Sparks), a Texas state diving champion in high school and later a physical-training instructor and high-school teacher, and Henry Nelson Elliott, who worked as a predator-control specialist for the [Department of the Interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Interior "United States Department of the Interior").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-4) His parents were originally from [El Paso, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso,_Texas "El Paso, Texas"), and Elliott has an ancestor who served as a surgeon at the [Battle of San Jacinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_San_Jacinto "Battle of San Jacinto").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-Slate-HollywoodOldWest-2015-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-7) He moved from California to [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"), with his family when he was 13 years old.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-hewitt-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-turnquist-9)

Elliott spent his teenage years living in [northeast Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighborhoods_of_Portland,_Oregon#Northeast "Neighborhoods of Portland, Oregon"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-hewitt-8) and graduated from [David Douglas High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Douglas_High_School "David Douglas High School") in 1962.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-turnquist-9) After graduating from high school, Elliott attended college at the [University of Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oregon "University of Oregon") as an English and psychology major[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-coen-10) for two terms before dropping out.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) He returned to [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon") and attended [Clark College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_College_(Washington) "Clark College (Washington)") in nearby [Vancouver, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver,_Washington "Vancouver, Washington"), where he completed a two-year program and was cast as Big Jule in a stage production of _[Guys and Dolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guys\_and\_Dolls "Guys and Dolls")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-hewitt-8) The Vancouver _[Columbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Columbian "The Columbian")_ newspaper suggested that Elliott should be a professional actor. After his graduation from Clark in 1965, Elliott re-enrolled at the University of Oregon and pledged at the [Sigma Alpha Epsilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigma_Alpha_Epsilon "Sigma Alpha Epsilon") fraternity.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) He dropped out again after his father died of a heart attack.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Sam_Elliott_college_yearbook_photo.jpg/250px-Sam_Elliott_college_yearbook_photo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sam_Elliott_college_yearbook_photo.jpg)

Elliott's 1965 college yearbook photo

In the late 1960s, Elliott relocated to Los Angeles to pursue a career in acting, which his father had dissuaded him from doing, instead urging him to obtain a college degree.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) "He gave me that proverbial line, 'You've got a snowball's chance in hell of having a career in (Hollywood),'" Elliott recalled. "He was a realist, my dad. He was a hard worker. He had a work ethic that I've fashioned mine after, and I thank him for that every day."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) Elliott worked in construction while studying acting and served in the [California Air National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Air_National_Guard "California Air National Guard")'s [146th Airlift Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/146th_Airlift_Wing "146th Airlift Wing") (the Hollywood Guard) at [Van Nuys Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Nuys_Airport "Van Nuys Airport") before the unit moved to Channel Islands Air National Guard Station in 1990.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-11)

## Career

### Early work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early work")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Juliet_Mills_and_Sam_Elliott_-_Once_an_Eagle.jpg/250px-Juliet_Mills_and_Sam_Elliott_-_Once_an_Eagle.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Juliet_Mills_and_Sam_Elliott_-_Once_an_Eagle.jpg)

Elliott with [Juliet Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juliet_Mills "Juliet Mills") in _[Once an Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once\_an\_Eagle\_(miniseries) "Once an Eagle (miniseries)")_ (1976)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Sam_Elliott_in_Lifeguard.jpg/250px-Sam_Elliott_in_Lifeguard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sam_Elliott_in_Lifeguard.jpg)

Elliott in his breakthrough role in _[Lifeguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifeguard\_(film) "Lifeguard (film)")_ (1976)

Elliott began his career as a [character actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_actor "Character actor"); his appearance, voice, and bearing were well-suited to [Westerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)"). In 1969, he earned his first television credit as Dan Kenyon in _[Judd for the Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judd\_for\_the\_Defense "Judd for the Defense")_ in the episode "The Crystal Maze".

That same year he appeared in the show _[Lancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancer\_(TV\_series) "Lancer (TV series)")_ in the episode "Death Bait", playing Renslo.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-complete-12) He went on to appear in two additional episodes of the series between 1970 and 1971.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-complete-12) One of his early film roles was as a [card player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Card_player "Card player") who watches as the Sundance Kid (Robert Redford) demonstrates his shooting ability in the opening scene of _[Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butch\_Cassidy\_and\_the\_Sundance\_Kid "Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid")_ (1969).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-tvg-13) In the 1970–1971 television season, Elliott starred as Doug Robert for several episodes in the hit series _[Mission: Impossible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_(1966\_TV\_series) "Mission: Impossible (1966 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-tvg-13) Beginning in 1972, Elliott appeared as the cowboy Walker in a series of Falstaff Beer commercials.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-16) In 1975, Elliott was cast in a lead role as [Charles Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Erskine_Scott_Wood "Charles Erskine Scott Wood") in the television film _[I Will Fight No More Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Will\_Fight\_No\_More\_Forever "I Will Fight No More Forever")_, a dramatization of Chief Joseph's resistance to the U.S. government's forcible removal of his Nez Perce Indian tribe to a reservation in Idaho.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-17)

From 1976 to 1977, he played the lead character Sam Damon in the miniseries _[Once an Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once\_an\_Eagle\_(miniseries) "Once an Eagle (miniseries)")_, an adaptation of the [Anton Myrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_Myrer "Anton Myrer")[novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once_An_Eagle "Once An Eagle"), opposite [Amy Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Irving "Amy Irving"), [Kim Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Hunter "Kim Hunter"), [Clu Gulager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clu_Gulager "Clu Gulager"), and [Melanie Griffith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melanie_Griffith "Melanie Griffith").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-18) He also had a starring role as Rick Carlson in the summer sleeper hit _[Lifeguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifeguard\_(film) "Lifeguard (film)")_ (1976), which marked his feature film breakthrough.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-davis-19) He portrayed a lifeguard in Southern California who reevaluates his life choices after being invited to a reunion.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-lgv-20)_Variety_ deemed the film "unsatisfying," adding: "Elliott, who has some beefcake value, projects a character who is mostly a passive reactor rather than a person in sure command of his fate."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-lgv-20)

### Recognition as a character actor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Recognition as a character actor")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Sam_Elliott_-_Aspen_still.jpg/250px-Sam_Elliott_-_Aspen_still.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sam_Elliott_-_Aspen_still.jpg)

Elliott in _Aspen_ (1977)

Elliott played Tom Keating in the miniseries _Aspen_ in 1977. He later played an abusive wife-killer in the miniseries _Murder in Texas_ (1981) opposite [Farrah Fawcett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farrah_Fawcett "Farrah Fawcett") and his future wife [Katharine Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katharine_Ross "Katharine Ross"),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-21) and starred with [Cheryl Ladd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Ladd "Cheryl Ladd") in _A Death in California_ (1985).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-22) In 1979, he co-starred with [Tom Selleck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Selleck "Tom Selleck") in the popular miniseries adaptation of [Louis L'Amour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_L'Amour "Louis L'Amour")'s _[The Sacketts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sacketts "The Sacketts")_. Elliott and Selleck were a team again in 1982 in _[The Shadow Riders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shadow\_Riders\_(film) "The Shadow Riders (film)")_, another Louis L'Amour adaption.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-match-23)

Elliott had a supporting role in _[Mask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mask\_(1985\_film) "Mask (1985 film)")_ (1985) opposite [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher "Cher"). He played a hard-nosed, rough-around-the-edges but ultimately sympathetic father figure in the Christmas film _[Prancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prancer\_(film) "Prancer (film)")_ (1989). He has made guest appearances on shows including _[Felony Squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felony\_Squad "Felony Squad")_, _[Gunsmoke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunsmoke "Gunsmoke")_, _[Lancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancer\_(TV\_series) "Lancer (TV series)")_, and _[Hawaii Five-O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii\_Five-O\_(1968\_TV\_series) "Hawaii Five-O (1968 TV series)")_, and has been featured in many TV movies, including _[Buffalo Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo\_Girls "Buffalo Girls")_ (1995), in which he played [Wild Bill Hickok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_Bill_Hickok "Wild Bill Hickok").

In 1986, he starred in the TV movie _[Gone to Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_to\_Texas\_(film) "Gone to Texas (film)")_, based on a biography of [Sam Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Houston "Sam Houston"). The role allowed him to play Houston as both fighter and a man who grew into a skillful political leader; the film depicted his disgrace as governor of Tennessee, his return to his [Cherokee Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee_Nation "Cherokee Nation") friends, and his pivotal role in the liberation of Texas from Mexico in 1836. Elliott appeared with [Patrick Swayze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Swayze "Patrick Swayze") in _[Road House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road\_House\_(1989\_film) "Road House (1989 film)")_ (1989) as Wade Garrett, a bouncer, mentor and friend of Swayze's character. In 1991, Elliott and his wife Katharine Ross starred in the adaptation of the [Louis L'Amour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_L'Amour "Louis L'Amour") novel _[Conagher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conagher "Conagher")_ (1991).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-24)

He portrayed [Brigadier General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigadier_general_(United_States) "Brigadier general (United States)")[John Buford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Buford "John Buford") in the 1993 historical drama _[Gettysburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gettysburg\_(1993\_film) "Gettysburg (1993 film)")_, and the same year played [Virgil Earp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil_Earp "Virgil Earp") in the Western _[Tombstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tombstone\_(film) "Tombstone (film)")_ (1993).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-afi-25) Elliott played The Stranger, a character narrating the story of _[The Big Lebowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Lebowski "The Big Lebowski")_ (1998).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-afi-25) He co-starred in _[We Were Soldiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_Were\_Soldiers "We Were Soldiers")_ (2002), an adaptation of _[We Were Soldiers Once… And Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_Were\_Soldiers\_Once%E2%80%A6\_And\_Young "We Were Soldiers Once… And Young")_, in which he portrayed [Command Sergeant Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command_Sergeant_Major "Command Sergeant Major")[Basil L. Plumley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basil_L._Plumley "Basil L. Plumley"). He played General [Thaddeus Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderbolt_Ross "Thunderbolt Ross") in the 2003 action film _[Hulk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulk\_(film) "Hulk (film)")_.

### Later career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Later career")]

In 2005, he appeared in _[Thank You for Smoking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Smoking\_(film) "Thank You for Smoking (film)")_ as a former [Marlboro Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlboro_Man "Marlboro Man") advertisement cowboy who has developed lung cancer. In 2006 he provided the voice for the character Ben the Cow in the animated film _[Barnyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnyard\_(film) "Barnyard (film)")_.

In 2007, Elliott joined the comic book adaptation _[Ghost Rider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_Rider\_(2007\_film) "Ghost Rider (2007 film)")_. He played the character [Carter Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Slade "Carter Slade"). The same year, Elliott appeared in _[The Golden Compass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Golden\_Compass\_(film) "The Golden Compass (film)")_ as the character Lee Scoresby. The film is based on _[Northern Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern\_Lights\_(Pullman\_novel) "Northern Lights (Pullman novel)")_ in [Philip Pullman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Pullman "Philip Pullman")'s trilogy _[His Dark Materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/His\_Dark\_Materials "His Dark Materials")_. Also appearing in the film are [Nicole Kidman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Kidman "Nicole Kidman"), [Christopher Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Lee "Christopher Lee"), and [Daniel Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Craig "Daniel Craig").

In 2009, Elliott had a small role in _[Up In The Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up\_in\_the\_Air\_(2009\_film) "Up in the Air (2009 film)")_ in which he portrayed the chief pilot of American Airlines. He appeared three times on _[Parks and Recreation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parks\_and\_Recreation "Parks and Recreation")_ as Ron Dunn, the Eagleton equivalent of [Ron Swanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Swanson "Ron Swanson"); Dunn is a hippie, compared to Swanson's staunch [survivalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survivalist "Survivalist") and [Libertarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian "Libertarian") personality. He then provided the voice of Buster (a.k.a. Chupadogra) in the animated film _[Marmaduke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marmaduke\_(2010\_film) "Marmaduke (2010 film)")_ (2010). He had a supporting role in the thriller film _[The Company You Keep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Company\_You\_Keep\_(film) "The Company You Keep (film)")_ and played a college football coach in 2014's drama film _[Draft Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft\_Day "Draft Day")_.

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Sam_Elliott_and_Jon_Hamm_%28Sundance_2017%29.jpg/250px-Sam_Elliott_and_Jon_Hamm_%28Sundance_2017%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sam_Elliott_and_Jon_Hamm_(Sundance_2017).jpg)

Elliott and [Jon Hamm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Hamm "Jon Hamm") at the 2017 [Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundance_Film_Festival "Sundance Film Festival")

In 2015, Elliott appeared opposite [Lily Tomlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Tomlin "Lily Tomlin") as a former love interest of a grandmother (Tomlin) attempting to help her pregnant granddaughter in [Paul Weitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Weitz_(filmmaker) "Paul Weitz (filmmaker)")'s comedy _[Grandma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grandma\_(2015\_film) "Grandma (2015 film)")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-NYTimes-Gma-AnatomyScene-2015-26) In the same year he appeared in the romance _[I'll See You in My Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll\_See\_You\_in\_My\_Dreams\_(2015\_film) "I'll See You in My Dreams (2015 film)")_, and had a role in the independent film _[Digging for Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digging\_for\_Fire "Digging for Fire")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-NYTimes-SamElliott-LeadingMan-2015-27) In 2015, he won the [Critics' Choice Television Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Television_Award "Critics' Choice Television Award") for best guest performer in a drama for his role in the [FX Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FX_Network "FX Network")'s show _[Justified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justified\_(TV\_series) "Justified (TV series)")_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-NYTimes-SamElliott-LeadingMan-2015-27)

### Career resurgence and critical acclaim

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Career resurgence and critical acclaim")]

In 2015, Elliott began appearing as a series regular in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") series _[The Ranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ranch\_(TV\_series) "The Ranch (TV series)")_, opposite [Ashton Kutcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashton_Kutcher "Ashton Kutcher") and [Danny Masterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Masterson "Danny Masterson").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-28) He also had a recurring role as Phil Millstein in the second season of _[Grace and Frankie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grace\_and\_Frankie "Grace and Frankie")_. In film, he supplied the voice of Butch in the animated film _[The Good Dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good\_Dinosaur "The Good Dinosaur")_ (2015).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-TGD-Recast-29)

In 2017, Elliott starred in _[The Hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hero\_(2017\_film) "The Hero (2017 film)")_, as Lee Hayden, an aging Western icon with a golden voice, whose best performances are decades behind him.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-30) His work in the film received much critical acclaim with Joey Magidson, writing for _AwardsCircuit_, proclaiming that "Elliott is perfect here. _The Hero_ encapsulates everything you love about him into one package."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-31) Later that year, Elliott starred in _[The Man Who Killed Hitler and Then the Bigfoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Man\_Who\_Killed\_Hitler\_and\_Then\_the\_Bigfoot "The Man Who Killed Hitler and Then the Bigfoot")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-32)

The following year, Elliott costarred in _[A Star Is Born](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Star\_Is\_Born\_(2018\_film) "A Star Is Born (2018 film)")_ (2018), in which he plays Bobby Maine, the elder half-brother of [Bradley Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_Cooper "Bradley Cooper")'s lead character.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-33) Elliott received critical acclaim for his performance, winning the [National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-nbr-34) He was also nominated for the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Male_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Supporting Role"), as well as the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor"), his career-first nomination.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-35) Commenting on his Academy Award nomination, Elliott declared: "I think the thing off the top of my head might be, 'It's about fucking time!'"[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-36) Since 2019, he played Wild West, new Mayor of Quahog, in 21 episodes of the animated series Family Guy. Wild West is a parody of Western film characters.

In 2022, Elliott starred as Shea Brennan on the [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") miniseries _[1883](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1883\_(TV\_series) "1883 (TV series)")_, a prequel to the _[Yellowstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone\_(American\_TV\_series) "Yellowstone (American TV series)")_ series. The show's story involves Brennan as he leads a group of immigrants from [Fort Worth, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth,_Texas "Fort Worth, Texas") into the untamed western areas of the plains, and its connection to the Dutton family and its migration to Montana. The show aired from late 2021 until February 2022. For his performance he received critical acclaim and won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Miniseries or Television Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Male_Actor_in_a_Miniseries_or_Television_Movie "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Miniseries or Television Movie").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-37)

In 2025, Elliott starred in the second season of the [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") series [_Landman_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landman_(TV_series) "Landman (TV series)"), as T. L. Norris, the father of the [Billy Bob Thornton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Bob_Thornton "Billy Bob Thornton")'s lead character.

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

In 1998, Elliott was named the grand marshal of the [Calgary Stampede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Stampede "Calgary Stampede") parade and rode in the [procession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Procession "Procession") before an estimated 300,000 spectators.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-38)

### Voice work and political endorsements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Voice work and political endorsements")]

Elliott has performed voice-over narration for various commercials. He has lent his voice to campaigns for [Dodge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodge "Dodge"), [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM"), [Kinney Drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinney_Drugs "Kinney Drugs"), [Union Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Pacific "Union Pacific"), and most notably the [American Beef Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Beef_Council "American Beef Council"), succeeding [Robert Mitchum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Mitchum "Robert Mitchum") in the latter. Since late 2007 Elliott has done voice-overs for [Coors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coors_Brewing_Company "Coors Brewing Company") beer, bringing his deep, rich voice and "western" appeal to the brand brewed in Colorado. In 2010, [Ram Trucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Trucks "Ram Trucks") hired Elliott to do the voice-over for their Ram Heavy Duty truck commercial; he has been voicing their commercials since. Starting in 2008, he has voiced [Smokey Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smokey_Bear "Smokey Bear"), and shares the mascot's birth date (August 9, 1944). He also narrated the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") and [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") team introductions to [Super Bowl XLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLV "Super Bowl XLV"), played at [Cowboys Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys_Stadium "Cowboys Stadium") in [Arlington, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_Texas "Arlington, Texas") at the conclusion of the [2010 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NFL_season "2010 NFL season") for _[NFL on Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL\_on\_Fox "NFL on Fox")_. On September 9, 2020, it was announced that Elliott would begin recurring on _[Family Guy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family\_Guy "Family Guy")_ as the new mayor of [Quahog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quahog,_Rhode_Island "Quahog, Rhode Island"), the late [Mayor Adam West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_West_(Family_Guy) "Adam West (Family Guy)")'s cousin, Wild Wild West.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-39) Also in 2020, he voiced [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden")'s "Go From There" [campaign ad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campaign_ad "Campaign ad").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-40) He did another ad for [The Lincoln Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lincoln_Project "The Lincoln Project"), in support of [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris")' [2024 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris_2024_presidential_campaign "Kamala Harris 2024 presidential campaign"), where he said "It's time to be a man and vote for a woman."

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Elliott married actress [Katharine Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katharine_Ross "Katharine Ross") in 1984, becoming her fifth husband.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-carvajal-41) They have a daughter, Cleo,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-42) who is a musician in [Malibu, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malibu,_California "Malibu, California").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-43) Ross and Elliott live in a seaside home in Malibu, which they purchased in the 1970s.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) Elliott also maintains a property in the [Willamette Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willamette_Valley "Willamette Valley") in Oregon.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3) Following his mother's death in 2011 at the age of 96, he also took ownership of his childhood home in northeast Portland.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott#cite_note-baker-3)

## Filmography and accolades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sam_Elliott&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Filmography and accolades")]

Main articles: [Sam Elliott filmography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott_filmography "Sam Elliott filmography") and [List of awards and nominations received by Sam Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Sam_Elliott "List of awards and nominations received by Sam Elliott")

Elliott has received [a number of awards and nominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Sam_Elliott "List of awards and nominations received by Sam Elliott") for [his numerous screen performances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Elliott_filmography "Sam Elliott filmography"). These include a [Screen Actors Guild Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award "Screen Actors Guild Award"), a [National Board of Review Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Awards "National Board of Review Awards") and nominations for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"), two [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") and two [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards").

After gaining early recognition in [western films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_films "Western films") in the late 1960s and continuing into the 1970s and 1980s, Elliott received two [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nominations—for [Best Actor in a Miniseries or Television Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_-_Miniseries_or_Television_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor - Miniseries or Television Film") and [Supporting Actor in a Series, Miniseries or Television Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor_-_Series,_Miniseries_or_Television_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor - Series, Miniseries or Television Film")—for his respective roles in the television film _[Conagher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conagher "Conagher")_ (1991) and miniseries _[Buffalo Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo\_Girls\_(miniseries) "Buffalo Girls (miniseries)")_ (1995), the latter of which also earned him a nomination for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Miniseries or Special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Supporting_Actor_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie"). His [voice-over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice-over "Voice-over") performance in _[Robot Chicken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robot\_Chicken "Robot Chicken")_ (2012–2020) earned him a nomination for the [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Voice-Over Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Voice-Over_Performance "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Voice-Over Performance"). Elliott's guest role in _[Justified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justified\_(TV\_series) "Justified (TV series)")_ (2015) earned him a [Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Guest Performer in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Television_Award_for_Best_Guest_Performer_in_a_Drama_Series "Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Guest Performer in a Drama Series").

As a member of the [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") of _[Up in the Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Up\_in\_the\_Air\_(2009\_film) "Up in the Air (2009 film)")_ (2009), Elliott was nominated for the [Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Acting Ensemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Movie_Award_for_Best_Acting_Ensemble "Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Acting Ensemble"). For starring opposite [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga") and [Bradley Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_Cooper "Bradley Cooper") in [Cooper's 2018 adaptation of _A Star Is Born_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Star_Is_Born_(2018_film) "A Star Is Born (2018 film)"), Elliott won the [National Board of Review Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor") and received nominations for the [AACTA International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AACTA_International_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "AACTA International Award for Best Supporting Actor"), [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor"), [Critics' Choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Movie_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Supporting Actor") and [SAG Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Male_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Supporting Role"), as well as another nomination for the [SAG Award for Outstanding Cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Cast_in_a_Motion_Picture "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture"). His role in the [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") miniseries _[1883](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1883\_(TV\_series) "1883 (TV series)")_ (2021–2022) won him the [SAG Award for Outstanding Actor in a Miniseries or Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Male_Actor_in_a_Miniseries_or_Television_Movie "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Miniseries or Television Movie").
