Aaliyah was raised in Detroit. She got her first major exposure appearing on the syndicated television series [Star Search (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085093/?ls), where she awed the audience with her amazing voice and talent, singing "My Funny Valentine", a song which her mother had sung years earlier. At age 11, she sang with [Gladys Knight](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0460912/?ls) in a five-night stint in Las Vegas. Withdrawing from the celebrity scene for a few years, Aaliyah lived the life of a normal teenage girl, attending Detroit's Performing Arts High School, where she majored in dance. It was around this same time that Aaliyah met singer/composer [R. Kelly](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005084/?ls). Kelly assisted Aaliyah with the production of her debut album "Age Ain't Nothing But A number", which scored several number hits, specifically "Back and Forth." The album's title was a brief reference to her short-lived marriage to [R. Kelly](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005084/?ls) (she was 15 years of age at the time, and he was in his 20s). Thir marriage was annulled due to her status as a minor.  
  
During her senior year, Aaliyah went on to record "One In A Million", which featured the songwriting talents of major R&B producers/writers [Missy Elliott](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1055396/?ls) and [Timbaland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0608856/?ls). The album was a major success and sealed Aaliyah's fame forever.  
  
Aaliyah recorded the single 'Journey to the past' for the [Anastasia (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118617/?ls) soundtrack. After seeing her at an awards show and in the video for her hit song "Are You that Somebody?" (from the [Eddie Murphy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000552/?ls) film [Doctor Dolittle (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118998/?ls)), film producer [Joel Silver](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005428/?ls) (producer of [The Matrix (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0133093/?ls) and other major actor films) asked Aaliyah to audition for a role in an romance/action film, [Romeo Must Die (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0165929/?ls). With her determination and sex appeal, Aaliyah won Silver over and was cast in her first major film role. [Romeo Must Die (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0165929/?ls) was a hit at the box office. This film led to her being cast as one of the stars of the film based on [Anne Rice](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0723351/?ls)'s [Queen of the Damned (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0238546/?ls), and in the two sequels to the major box office hit, [The Matrix (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0133093/?ls), [The Matrix Reloaded (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0234215/?ls) and [The Matrix Revolutions (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0242653/?ls).  
  
During the busy schedule of her film career, Aaliyah took time to record her third album, the self-titled "Aaliyah". July 2001 was a busy time for Aaliyah. After the success of her song "Try Again", for which she was nominated for a Grammy Award and won several MTV Video Awards, Aaliyah finally released her "Aaliyah" album. Debuting at number two on the Billboard charts, "Aaliyah" was a sales success, despite some lackluster reviews.  
  
In August 2001, Aaliyah took time off from her busy album promotional tour to fly to the Bahamas to film a video for the song "Rock the Boat". The video, filmed on Abaco Island, was directed by [Hype Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0930782/?ls), a major music video director known for his style and wit.  
  
On August 25, 2001, after filming the video, Aaliyah and about 9-11 of her entourage took off from Marsh Harbour airport at 6:50pm EDT in a small Cessna 404 en route to Opa-Locka, Florida. A few minutes after take-off, the plane crashed about 200 feet from the runaway, killing Aaliyah and many others instantly. Four passengers were pulled alive from the wreckage, and one later died at a hospital in Nassau. Aaliyah was only 22 years old. Her funeral was held on Friday August 31st in New York, and 22 white doves were flown to celebrate each year of her life. Soon after her death, the hit singles 'More Than a woman' and 'Rock The Boat' were released, from her third album. In 2002, the film [Queen of the Damned (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0238546/?ls) was released, in which Aaliyah played Queen Akasha. She was nominated for best Villain at the MTV Movie Awards 2002.  
  
Aaliyah's short-lived, but brilliant career, was a true success story for a young African-American woman who went against all odds to be herself in an industry where originality is scarce. Truly missed by her family, friends, and fans, her music and film contributions will live forever. It's no wonder that her name means 'Highest, most ex-halted one; the best' in Hebrew. She had achieved so much in her twenty-two years.

But it was the memorial his friends held at the Public Theater that revealed the most about the actor. On a hot, sticky July afternoon, dozens of Pierce's tight family of skaters converged a few blocks uptown from the skateboard store Supreme, where Pierce was a fixture. As "Knocking on Heaven's Door" played over the sound system, the crowd wept openly while friends rose to memorialize Pierce.

On July 10, 2000, aged 25, Pierce was discovered hanged in his room at the Bellagio Hotel by hotel security. His death was a determined to be a suicide

British actor David Rappaport earned more roles and respect than most guys his size (or any size for that matter) who attempted a professional acting career. Born with the genetic condition dwarfism (he was 3' 11"), he was often typecast in bizarre, sometimes silly and demeaning roles; but, like others before ([Michael Dunn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0242692/?ls)) and after ([Peter Dinklage](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0227759/?ls)), he rose to the challenge and proved himself a talent to be reckoned with.  
  
He was born David Stephen Rappaport on November 23, 1951, to a London Jewish family and showed musical prowess at an early age. He learned how to play both the drums and the accordion, which helped him out financially during the lean years. He studied psychology at the University of Bristol in 1969 and graduated with a degree while developing a side interest in theatre and performing in plays and revues. Following graduation, he married his college girlfriend, Jane, and had a son, Joe, the following year. He gave school teaching a try but left in 1977 to focus on his first love - acting.  
  
Returning to England, he built up his reputation on TV and developed celebrity status. He acted in and wrote for the program "Beyond the Groove" and performed in a couple of children's series to boot. Film showcases for David came unexpectedly with the scene-stealing role of "Randall", the ringleader of a motley group of time-traveling thieves, in [Time Bandits (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081633/?ls), and in [The Bride (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0088851/?ls) as "Rinaldo", a little person who befriends a giant. American audiences were given a good taste of David's charm, intelligence and razor-sharp wit with the popular but short-lived series, [The Wizard (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090547/?ls), as "Simon McKay", the inventor of odd and exciting toys who derived great pleasure out of being a good Samaritan. He followed this with the attention-getting role of slick attorney "Hamilton Skylar" in a few episodes of [L.A. Law (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090466/?ls).  
  
Despite his successful professional career, David was beset by personal unhappiness and acute depression. He was booked to play the darkly comic role of Zibalian trader Kivas Fajo on "Star Trek: The Next Generation" (episode "The Most Toys," subsequently played by gifted Canadian actor [Saul Rubinek](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007210/?ls)). However, on May 2, 1990, Rappaport's third suicide attempt was successful, as he shot himself in the chest with a .38 caliber revolver he had bought 15 days earlier. The 38-year-old actor was buried at the Waltham Abbey cemetery in England.

Rappaport struggled with depression later in his life. On May 2, 1990, he committed suicide by shooting himself in the chest in Laurel Canyon Park in the San Fernando Valley, California.

[![Image 17: Italian epstain Credits: Savoy Pictures / Directed by Robert De Niro, written by Chazz Palminteri (based on his play), starring Robert De Niro, Chazz Palminteri, Lillo Brancato, Francis Capra. A Bronx Tale (1993) is a coming-of-age crime drama set in the 1960s Bronx, following Calogero, a young Italian-American boy torn between two father figures: his honest, hardworking bus-driver father Lorenzo (Robert De Niro) and charismatic local mob boss Sonny (Chazz Palminteri). After Calogero witnesses a crime and chooses not to identify Sonny, he earns the gangster’s respect and is gradually drawn into that world. The film explores loyalty, masculinity, race relations, and the moral crossroads between easy power and honest struggle. [![Image 15: This is one of Robert De Niro’s most underrated films. Robert De Niro steps behind the camera for the first time with A Bronx Tale (1993), and he absolutely nails it. This isn’t just another gangster movie it’s a deeply personal story about growing up torn between two worlds. Robert De Niro plays Lorenzo, a hardworking bus driver trying to raise his son right in a neighborhood where the local mobster, Sonny (Chazz Palminteri), holds more sway than any father ever could. Young Calogero is caught in the middle, drawn to Sonny’s power and respect while his father preaches honest work and integrity. [![Image 17: Italian epstain Credits: Savoy Pictures / Directed by Robert De Niro, written by Chazz Palminteri (based on his play), starring Robert De Niro, Chazz Palminteri, Lillo Brancato, Francis Capra. A Bronx Tale (1993) is a coming-of-age crime drama set in the 1960s Bronx, following Calogero, a young Italian-American boy torn between two father figures: his honest, hardworking bus-driver father Lorenzo (Robert De Niro) and charismatic local mob boss Sonny (Chazz Palminteri). After Calogero witnesses a crime and chooses not to identify Sonny, he earns the gangster’s respect and is gradually drawn into that world. The film explores loyalty, masculinity, race relations, and the moral crossroads between easy power and honest struggle. Rather than glamorizing mob life, the story focuses on values—what it means to be a man, how environment shapes identity, and the quiet strength of integrity. The “working man vs. gangster” contrast is the emotional core of the film. [![Image 21: A Bronx Tale (1993) was Robert De Niro’s directorial debut. [![Image 17: Italian epstain Credits: Savoy Pictures / Directed by Robert De Niro, written by Chazz Palminteri (based on his play), starring Robert De Niro, Chazz Palminteri, Lillo Brancato, Francis Capra. A Bronx Tale (1993) is a coming-of-age crime drama set in the 1960s Bronx, following Calogero, a young Italian-American boy torn between two father figures: his honest, hardworking bus-driver father Lorenzo (Robert De Niro) and charismatic local mob boss Sonny (Chazz Palminteri). After Calogero witnesses a crime and chooses not to identify Sonny, he earns the gangster’s respect and is gradually drawn into that world. The film explores loyalty, masculinity, race relations, and the moral crossroads between easy power and honest struggle. Actress Lea Moreno got her start in community theater in Orange County. She studied at South Coast Repertory for ten years before landing her first screen roles shortly after graduating from high school. In 1995, her tenth and eleventh auditions landed her guest roles on the ABC sitcoms "Home Improvement" and "Step by Step". The following year, she made her TV-movie debut co-starring alongside Jonathan Brandis, Ariana Richards and Christopher Noth in the ABC movie "Born Free: A New Adventure". Moreno and Brandis played city kids who move with their businessman father to Africa, where they endeavor to return a captured lion to the wild. That same year she made her feature acting debut in a similar setting, the safari-set Tarzan retread "Jungle Boy" (a 1998 US direct-to-video release).  
  
More TV work followed for Moreno, who guest starred on series including "Promised Land" and "Walker, Texas Ranger" (both CBS) and a recurring on "Clueless" (UPN) playing the snobby cheerleader Brittany. Additionally, she was featured as the daughter of a breast cancer survivor (Mary McDonnell) whose health is once again in jeopardy in "Two Voices", Lifetime's 1997 fact-based account of the class-action suit that rocked the silicone breast implant industry. Moreno followed up this supporting role with a starring turn as the leader of a group of heroic children navigating a post-apocalyptic lost world battling an evil-doer (Tim Curry) in Showtime's sci-fi original "Doom Runners" (also 1997). From 1998 to 1999, Moreno starred on the UPN hour-long drama "Legacy" as Alice Logan, a conscientious young teenager who takes over as the Logan's maternal force following her mother's untimely death. Moreno performed well in the role, winning over audiences as she portrayed Alice's shortcomings as well as her grace and indomitable spirit. Following the cancellation of the 19th Century American Reconstruction era serial, Moreno had a memorable lead guest role as a teenager meeting her father for the first time on a special two-hour Thanksgiving episode of NBC's hit drama "Providence" (1999). The following year the young actress returned to series television on The WB's quirky mid-season replacement sitcom "Brutally Normal" from the producers of "Popular." Here she took on the role of Anna Pricova, a smart and passionate high school student who was dealing with the ever ready trials of teenage life and the messes caused by her two troublesome best friends (Eddie Kaye Thomas and Mike Damus).  
  
In 2000 Moreno landed the lead in an NBC pilot titled "Just Married", written by Jack Burditt of "30 Rock" and "Just Shoot Me" fame. She starred opposite Chris Evans ("Captain America" and "The Avengers") in this comedy about the trials and tribulations of getting married at a young age. The pilot did not go to series but NBC liked Moreno enough to ask her to join the cast of "D.A.G." playing Camilla Whitman, daughter of the President of the United States and First Lady. This multi-camera comedy, with an outstanding ensemble cast (David Alan Grier, Delta Burke, Lauren Tom, Paul F. Tompkins) only lasted one season but was a bright spot for Moreno as she held her own with some of TV comedies funniest, playing a sassy and smart, overly protected first daughter.  
  
In 2003 Moreno landed supporting roles in two independent films. "Last Stand" and "Demon Hunter." The next few years followed with more supporting roles in independents as well as a lead guest star on the popular series "CSI Miami." Moreno played Kim/Demon leader of a gang of gamers that will stop at nothing to get what they want. In 2007 she starred in another popular series "Monk." In 2010 and 2011 Moreno and her husband Chris Young (Max Headroom, Great Outdoors, PCU) produced "Dead of Nowhere", a 3D feature film presentation starring Balthazar Getty and Lin Shaye.  
  
2013 and 2014 saw a welcome change in Moreno's career, back to back roles playing a young mother. She co-starred in a feature film, "Sins of Our Youth", playing a young mom upset by the loss of her son to gun violence and then a guest star on the long running CBS hit, CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, playing Karen Lewis, a wealthy, troubled young mother in rehab.  
  
Lea resides in Los Angeles with her husband and their two daughters.

Actress Lea Moreno got her start in community theater in Orange County. She studied at South Coast Repertory for ten years before landing her first screen roles shortly after graduating from high school. In 1995, her tenth and eleventh auditions landed her guest roles on the ABC sitcoms "Home Improvement" and "Step by Step". The following year, she made her TV-movie debut co-starring alongside Jonathan Brandis, Ariana Richards and Christopher Noth in the ABC movie "Born Free: A New Adventure". Moreno and Brandis played city kids who move with their businessman father to Africa, where they endeavor to return a captured lion to the wild. That same year she made her feature acting debut in a similar setting, the safari-set Tarzan retread "Jungle Boy" (a 1998 US direct-to-video release).  
  
More TV work followed for Moreno, who guest starred on series including "Promised Land" and "Walker, Texas Ranger" (both CBS) and a recurring on "Clueless" (UPN) playing the snobby cheerleader Brittany. Additionally, she was featured as the daughter of a breast cancer survivor (Mary McDonnell) whose health is once again in jeopardy in "Two Voices", Lifetime's 1997 fact-based account of the class-action suit that rocked the silicone breast implant industry. Moreno followed up this supporting role with a starring turn as the leader of a group of heroic children navigating a post-apocalyptic lost world battling an evil-doer (Tim Curry) in Showtime's sci-fi original "Doom Runners" (also 1997). From 1998 to 1999, Moreno starred on the UPN hour-long drama "Legacy" as Alice Logan, a conscientious young teenager who takes over as the Logan's maternal force following her mother's untimely death. Moreno performed well in the role, winning over audiences as she portrayed Alice's shortcomings as well as her grace and indomitable spirit. Following the cancellation of the 19th Century American Reconstruction era serial, Moreno had a memorable lead guest role as a teenager meeting her father for the first time on a special two-hour Thanksgiving episode of NBC's hit drama "Providence" (1999). The following year the young actress returned to series television on The WB's quirky mid-season replacement sitcom "Brutally Normal" from the producers of "Popular." Here she took on the role of Anna Pricova, a smart and passionate high school student who was dealing with the ever ready trials of teenage life and the messes caused by her two troublesome best friends (Eddie Kaye Thomas and Mike Damus).  
  
In 2000 Moreno landed the lead in an NBC pilot titled "Just Married", written by Jack Burditt of "30 Rock" and "Just Shoot Me" fame. She starred opposite Chris Evans ("Captain America" and "The Avengers") in this comedy about the trials and tribulations of getting married at a young age. The pilot did not go to series but NBC liked Moreno enough to ask her to join the cast of "D.A.G." playing Camilla Whitman, daughter of the President of the United States and First Lady. This multi-camera comedy, with an outstanding ensemble cast (David Alan Grier, Delta Burke, Lauren Tom, Paul F. Tompkins) only lasted one season but was a bright spot for Moreno as she held her own with some of TV comedies funniest, playing a sassy and smart, overly protected first daughter.  
  
In 2003 Moreno landed supporting roles in two independent films. "Last Stand" and "Demon Hunter." The next few years followed with more supporting roles in independents as well as a lead guest star on the popular series "CSI Miami." Moreno played Kim/Demon leader of a gang of gamers that will stop at nothing to get what they want. In 2007 she starred in another popular series "Monk." In 2010 and 2011 Moreno and her husband Chris Young (Max Headroom, Great Outdoors, PCU) produced "Dead of Nowhere", a 3D feature film presentation starring Balthazar Getty and Lin Shaye.  
  
2013 and 2014 saw a welcome change in Moreno's career, back to back roles playing a young mother. She co-starred in a feature film, "Sins of Our Youth", playing a young mom upset by the loss of her son to gun violence and then a guest star on the long running CBS hit, CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, playing Karen Lewis, a wealthy, troubled young mother in rehab.  
  
Lea resides in Los Angeles with her husband and their two daughters.

# Lea Moreno

Highest Rated: Not Available

Lowest Rated: Not Available

Birthday: Nov 10, 1977

Birthplace: Chambersburg, Pennsylvania, USA

A pretty brunette with striking wide eyes and a compelling screen presence, actress Lea Moreno got her start in community theater then started acting at the West Coast Performing Arts Center and South Coast Repertory before landing her first screen roles shortly after graduating from high school. In 1995, she had guest roles on the ABC sitcoms "Home Improvement" and "Step by Step." The following year, she made her TV-movie debut co-starring alongside Jonathan Brandis, Ariana Richards and Christopher Noth in the ABC movie "Born Free: A New Adventure." Moreno and Brandis played city kids who move with their businessman father to Africa, where they endeavor to return a captured lion to the wild. That same year she made her feature acting debut in a similar setting, the safari-set Tarzan retread "Jungle Boy" (a 1998 US direct-to-video release). More TV work followed for Moreno, who guest starred on series including "Promised Land" and "Walker, Texas Ranger" (both CBS) and "Clueless" (UPN). Additionally, she was featured as the daughter of a breast cancer survivor (Mary McDonnell) whose health is once again in jeopardy in "Two Voices," Lifetime's 1997 fact-based account of the class-action suit that rocked the silicone breast implant industry. Moreno followed up this supporting role with a starring turn as the leader of a group of heroic children navigating a post-apocalyptic lost world in Showtime's sci-fi original "Doom Runners" (also 1997).

# Lea Moreno

Highest Rated: Not Available

Lowest Rated: Not Available

Birthday: Nov 10, 1977

Birthplace: Chambersburg, Pennsylvania, USA

A pretty brunette with striking wide eyes and a compelling screen presence, actress Lea Moreno got her start in community theater then started acting at the West Coast Performing Arts Center and South Coast Repertory before landing her first screen roles shortly after graduating from high school. In 1995, she had guest roles on the ABC sitcoms "Home Improvement" and "Step by Step." The following year, she made her TV-movie debut co-starring alongside Jonathan Brandis, Ariana Richards and Christopher Noth in the ABC movie "Born Free: A New Adventure." Moreno and Brandis played city kids who move with their businessman father to Africa, where they endeavor to return a captured lion to the wild. That same year she made her feature acting debut in a similar setting, the safari-set Tarzan retread "Jungle Boy" (a 1998 US direct-to-video release). More TV work followed for Moreno, who guest starred on series including "Promised Land" and "Walker, Texas Ranger" (both CBS) and "Clueless" (UPN). Additionally, she was featured as the daughter of a breast cancer survivor (Mary McDonnell) whose health is once again in jeopardy in "Two Voices," Lifetime's 1997 fact-based account of the class-action suit that rocked the silicone breast implant industry. Moreno followed up this supporting role with a starring turn as the leader of a group of heroic children navigating a post-apocalyptic lost world in Showtime's sci-fi original "Doom Runners" (also 1997).

# Lea Moreno

From 1998 to 1999, Moreno starred on the UPN hour-long drama "Legacy" as Alice Logan, a conscientious young teenager who takes over as the Logan's maternal force following her mother's untimely death. Saddled with a willful younger sister, two ambitious older brothers and preoccupied father, Alice struggled to balance her family obligations with her burgeoning womanhood, interest in feminist causes, and budding romance with Jeremy, a teenage boy adopted into the family. Moreno performed well in the role, winning over audiences as she portrayed Alice's shortcomings as well as her grace and indomitable spirit. Following the cancellation of the 19th Century American Reconstruction era serial, Moreno had a memorable guest role as a teenager meeting her father for the first time on a special two-hour Thanksgiving episode of NBC's hit drama "Providence" (1999). The following year the young actress returned to series television on The WB's quirky midseason replacement sitcom "Brutally Normal." Here she took on the role of Anna Pricova, a smart and passionate high school student who, along with the like-minded Dru (Tangie Ambrose), was dealing with the Eveready trials of teenage life and the messes caused by her two troublesome best friends Russell (Eddie Kaye Thomas) and Pooh (Mike Damus).

# Lea Moreno

From 1998 to 1999, Moreno starred on the UPN hour-long drama "Legacy" as Alice Logan, a conscientious young teenager who takes over as the Logan's maternal force following her mother's untimely death. Saddled with a willful younger sister, two ambitious older brothers and preoccupied father, Alice struggled to balance her family obligations with her burgeoning womanhood, interest in feminist causes, and budding romance with Jeremy, a teenage boy adopted into the family. Moreno performed well in the role, winning over audiences as she portrayed Alice's shortcomings as well as her grace and indomitable spirit. Following the cancellation of the 19th Century American Reconstruction era serial, Moreno had a memorable guest role as a teenager meeting her father for the first time on a special two-hour Thanksgiving episode of NBC's hit drama "Providence" (1999). The following year the young actress returned to series television on The WB's quirky midseason replacement sitcom "Brutally Normal." Here she took on the role of Anna Pricova, a smart and passionate high school student who, along with the like-minded Dru (Tangie Ambrose), was dealing with the Eveready trials of teenage life and the messes caused by her two troublesome best friends Russell (Eddie Kaye Thomas) and Pooh (Mike Damus).

**Rita Moreno** (born **Rosa Dolores Alverío Marcano**;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-1) December 11, 1931) is a Puerto Rican actress, dancer, and singer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-2) With a career spanning eight decades, she is known for her roles on stage and screen, and is one of the last remaining stars from the [Golden Age of Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Age_of_Hollywood "Golden Age of Hollywood"). Among her [numerous accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Rita_Moreno "List of awards and nominations received by Rita Moreno"), she is one of the few actors to have been awarded an [Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar, and a Tony (EGOT)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EGOT "EGOT")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-4) and the [Triple Crown of Acting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_Crown_of_Acting "Triple Crown of Acting").[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-5) She has been honored with [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom") in 2004, the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts") in 2009, the [Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Life_Achievement_Award "Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award") in 2013, the [Kennedy Center Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") in 2015, and a [Peabody Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Award "Peabody Award") in 2019.

Moreno's early work included supporting roles in the classic musical films _[Singin' in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singin'\_in\_the\_Rain "Singin' in the Rain")_ (1952) and _[The King and I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_King\_and\_I\_(1956\_film) "The King and I (1956 film)")_ (1956), before her breakout role as Anita in _[West Side Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West\_Side\_Story\_(1961\_film) "West Side Story (1961 film)")_ (1961), which earned her the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress"), making her the first [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic "Hispanic") woman to win an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-6) Moreno returned in the supporting role of Valentina in the 2021 [Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")-directed [remake of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side_Story_(2021_film) "West Side Story (2021 film)"). Her other films include _[Popi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popi "Popi")_ (1969), _[Carnal Knowledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnal\_Knowledge\_(film) "Carnal Knowledge (film)")_ (1971), _[The Four Seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Seasons\_(1981\_film) "The Four Seasons (1981 film)")_ (1981), _[I Like It Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Like\_It\_Like\_That\_(film) "I Like It Like That (film)")_ (1994), _[Slums of Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slums\_of\_Beverly\_Hills "Slums of Beverly Hills")_ (1998), and _[Fast X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_X "Fast X")_ (2023).

In theater, she starred as Googie Gomez in the 1975 [Terrence McNally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_McNally "Terrence McNally") musical _[The Ritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ritz\_(play) "The Ritz (play)")_ earning her the [Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play"). She reprised her role in the [1976 film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ritz_(film) "The Ritz (film)") directed by [Richard Lester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Lester "Richard Lester") which earned her a [BAFTA Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Leading_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role") nomination. She also acted in [Lorraine Hansberry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorraine_Hansberry "Lorraine Hansberry")'s _[The Sign in Sidney Brustein's Window](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sign\_in\_Sidney\_Brustein's\_Window "The Sign in Sidney Brustein's Window")_ in 1964 and in [Neil Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Simon "Neil Simon")'s _[The Odd Couple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Odd\_Couple\_(play) "The Odd Couple (play)")_ in 1985.

She was a cast member in _[The Electric Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Electric\_Company "The Electric Company")_ (1971–1977), for which she earned an Grammy for Best Album for Children in 1972, and played Sister Peter Marie Reimondo on the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") series _[Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_(TV\_series) "Oz (TV series)")_ (1997–2003). She received two consecutive [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") for her roles on _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_ in 1977 and _[The Rockford Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rockford\_Files "The Rockford Files")_ in 1978. She acted in _[Where on Earth Is Carmen Sandiego?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where\_on\_Earth\_Is\_Carmen\_Sandiego%3F "Where on Earth Is Carmen Sandiego?")_ (1994–1999), [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW") series _[Jane the Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_the\_Virgin "Jane the Virgin")_ (2015–2019), and the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") revival of _[One Day at a Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Day\_at\_a\_Time\_(2017\_series) "One Day at a Time (2017 series)")_ (2017–2020). Her life was profiled in _[Rita Moreno: Just a Girl Who Decided to Go for It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita\_Moreno:\_Just\_a\_Girl\_Who\_Decided\_to\_Go\_for\_It "Rita Moreno: Just a Girl Who Decided to Go for It")_ (2021).

## Early years

Rita Moreno was born Rosa Dolores Alverío Marcano, on December 11, 1931, in a [Humacao, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humacao "Humacao"), hospital to Rosa María (née Marcano) (1912–1999), a seamstress, and Francisco José "Paco" Alverío, a farmer who was born in 1908. Her parents divorced the following year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera141-7) She was nicknamed "Rosita" and raised in nearby [Juncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juncos,_Puerto_Rico "Juncos, Puerto Rico").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-autobio-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-filmr-9) Her maternal grandparents were Justino Marcano (b. Puerto Rico) and Trinidad from Spain.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-10)

Moreno's mother moved to New York City in 1936, taking her daughter, but not her son, Moreno's younger brother, Francisco, whom Moreno would not see again until 2021.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-The_View-11) Moreno adopted the surname of her first stepfather, Edward Moreno, Rosa Maria's second husband. She spent her teenage years living in the NYC suburb of [Valley Stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valley_Stream,_New_York "Valley Stream, New York") on [Long Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Island "Long Island").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-12)

## Career

### 1945–1959: Theater debut and early films

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Rita-Moreno-1.jpg/250px-Rita-Moreno-1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rita-Moreno-1.jpg)

Rita Moreno in 1954

Moreno began her first dancing lessons soon after arriving in New York with a Spanish dancer known as "Paco Cansino", who was a paternal uncle of film star [Rita Hayworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Hayworth "Rita Hayworth").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-13) When she was 11 years old, she lent her voice to Spanish-language versions of American films.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera95-14) She had her first [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") role, as "Angelina" in the 1945 production of _Skydrift_, by the age of 13, which caught the attention of Hollywood talent scouts. Moreno said she was raped by her agent while she was a teen actor.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-16)

Moreno's film career began in the later years of the [Golden Age of Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Age_of_Hollywood "Golden Age of Hollywood"). Moreno and her mother moved to a Culver City "cottage" within walking distance of [MGM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM "MGM").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-17) After signing a contract, Moreno began her cinema career, performing under the name of "Rosita Moreno".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera142-18) MGM had her first name abbreviated to Rita.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera142-18) Her first film was _So Young, So Bad_ (1950).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera142-18) Moreno's contract with MGM was cut short, after which she found work in films independently.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera142-18) She acted steadily in films throughout the 1950s, usually in small roles, including in _[The Toast of New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Toast\_of\_New\_Orleans "The Toast of New Orleans")_ (1950).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-19) In 1952, she appeared in [Stanley Donen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Donen "Stanley Donen")'s musical comedy film _[Singin' in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singin'\_in\_the\_Rain "Singin' in the Rain")_ alongside [Gene Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Kelly "Gene Kelly"), [Debbie Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Reynolds "Debbie Reynolds") and [Donald O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_O'Connor "Donald O'Connor"). In the film she played silent film star Zelda Zanders. She described having gotten the role by Gene Kelly "wanting her in the movie" and that she "seemed to fit the role for him". Moreno praised Kelly for casting her in a non-stereotypical Hispanic role playing Zelda saying, "he never said 'Oh she's too Latina', he just thought I'd be fine for it". She called the experience working in the film as an "amazing experience" and a "privilege".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-20)

In March 1954, Moreno was featured on the cover of _Life_ magazine with the caption "Rita Moreno: An Actress's Catalog of Sex and Innocence".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-berkeleyside.com-21) She was the first Puerto Rican featured in this publication.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera95-14) Moreno disliked most of her film work during this period, as she felt the roles she was given were very stereotypical. One exception was her supporting role in the film version of [Rodgers and Hammerstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodgers_and_Hammerstein "Rodgers and Hammerstein")'s _[The King and I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_King\_and\_I\_(1956\_film) "The King and I (1956 film)")_ directed by [Walter Lang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Lang "Walter Lang"). In the film she played Tuptim, a slave brought from Burma to be one of the King's junior wives.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-IMDB-22) She starred alongside [Yul Brynner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yul_Brynner "Yul Brynner") and [Deborah Kerr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deborah_Kerr "Deborah Kerr"). The film was a critical and financial success. It received nine [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nominations including five wins including [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor"), [Best Art Direction – Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Production_Design "Academy Award for Best Production Design"), [Best Costume Design – Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Costume_Design "Academy Award for Best Costume Design"), [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Academy Award for Best Original Score"), and [Best Sound Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound "Academy Award for Best Sound"). In 1959, Moreno appeared as [Lola Montez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lola_Montez "Lola Montez") in Season 3, Episode 23, of the TV western _[Tales of Wells Fargo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tales\_of\_Wells\_Fargo "Tales of Wells Fargo")_, episode title "Lola Montez".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-23)

### 1960–1969: Breakout with _West Side Story_

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/West_Side_Story_%281961%29_still_2.jpg/250px-West_Side_Story_%281961%29_still_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:West_Side_Story_(1961)_still_2.jpg)

Moreno as Anita in _[West Side Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West\_Side\_Story\_(1961\_film) "West Side Story (1961 film)")_

In 1961, Moreno landed the role of Anita in [Robert Wise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wise "Robert Wise") and [Jerome Robbins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Robbins "Jerome Robbins")' film adaptation of [Leonard Bernstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Bernstein "Leonard Bernstein")'s and [Stephen Sondheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Sondheim "Stephen Sondheim")'s groundbreaking [Broadway musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_musical "Broadway musical")_[West Side Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West\_Side\_Story\_(1961\_film) "West Side Story (1961 film)")_, which had been played by [Chita Rivera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chita_Rivera "Chita Rivera") on Broadway. Moreno earned acclaim for her performance. Bosley Crowther of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ described Moreno's performance full of "spitfire".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-24)_[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ wrote, "Moreno...presents a fiery characterization and also scores hugely".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-25) The film went on to win ten [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") including for [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). Moreno won the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") for that role.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-RM-26)

After winning the Oscar, Moreno thought she would be able to continue to perform less stereotypical film roles, but was disappointed:

> Ha, ha. I showed them. I didn't make another movie for seven years after winning the Oscar.... Before _West Side Story_, I was always offered the stereotypical Latina roles. The Conchitas and Lolitas in westerns. I was always barefoot. It was humiliating, embarrassing stuff. But I did it because there was nothing else. After _West Side Story_, it was pretty much the same thing. A lot of gang stories.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-27)

Moreno became frustrated with the situation and left to London, where she joined the cast of _She Loves Me_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera143-28) Due to work limitations for foreigners in the United Kingdom, she returned to Broadway in _The Sign in Sidney Brustein's Window_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera143-28)

Moreno had a major role in _[Summer and Smoke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer\_and\_Smoke\_(film) "Summer and Smoke (film)")_ (1961), released soon after _West Side Story_. She did appear in one film during her self-imposed exile from Hollywood– _[Cry of Battle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cry\_of\_Battle "Cry of Battle")_ (1963)– although it had been filmed directly before and after she won the Academy Award. She made her return to film in _[The Night of the Following Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Night\_of\_the\_Following\_Day "The Night of the Following Day")_ (1968) with [Marlon Brando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlon_Brando "Marlon Brando"), and followed that with _[Popi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popi "Popi")_ (1969), and _[Marlowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlowe\_(1969\_film) "Marlowe (1969 film)")_ (1969) with [James Garner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Garner "James Garner"). Moreno's Broadway credits include _[Last of the Red Hot Lovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last\_of\_the\_Red\_Hot\_Lovers "Last of the Red Hot Lovers")_ (1969), the musical _[Gantry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gantry\_(musical) "Gantry (musical)")_ (1970), and _[The Ritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ritz\_(play) "The Ritz (play)")_, for which she won the 1975 [Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play"). She appeared in the female version of _[The Odd Couple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Female\_Odd\_Couple "The Female Odd Couple")_[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-IMDB-22) that ran in Chicago, for which she won the [Sarah Siddons Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Siddons_Award "Sarah Siddons Award") in 1985.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-RM-26) Her costar [Sally Struthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sally_Struthers "Sally Struthers") later stated in an interview on _[Gilbert Gottfried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert\_Gottfried "Gilbert Gottfried")'s Amazing Colossal Podcast_ that it was an unpleasant experience until Rita Moreno, who Struthers alleges was mean-spirited towards her, left the play and was replaced by [Brenda Vaccaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brenda_Vaccaro "Brenda Vaccaro").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-29)

### 1970–1999: Established actress

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Rita_Moreno_in_The_Ritz_%281975%29.jpg/250px-Rita_Moreno_in_The_Ritz_%281975%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rita_Moreno_in_The_Ritz_(1975).jpg)

Moreno in _[The Ritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ritz\_(film) "The Ritz (film)")_ in 1975

From 1971 to 1977, Moreno was a main cast member on the [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS") children's series _[The Electric Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Electric\_Company "The Electric Company")_. She screamed the show's opening line, "Hey, you guys!" Her roles on the show included Millie the Helper, the naughty little girl Pandora, and [Otto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_The_Director "Otto The Director"), a very short-tempered director. Moreno also starred in [Mike Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Nichols "Mike Nichols")' _[Carnal Knowledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnal\_Knowledge\_(film) "Carnal Knowledge (film)")_ (1971) alongside [Jack Nicholson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nicholson "Jack Nicholson"), [Candice Bergen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candice_Bergen "Candice Bergen"), [Ann-Margret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann-Margret "Ann-Margret"), and [Art Garfunkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Garfunkel "Art Garfunkel"). In the film she plays a prostitute named Louise, whom Jack Nicholson plays cards with. The film was a critical success. In 1976 she starred as Googie Gomez in [Richard Lester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Lester "Richard Lester")'s film adaptation of the comedy [farce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farce "Farce")_[The Ritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ritz\_(film) "The Ritz (film)")_ alongside [Jack Weston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Weston "Jack Weston"), [Jerry Stiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Stiller "Jerry Stiller"), and [F. Murray Abraham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F._Murray_Abraham "F. Murray Abraham"). [Charles Champlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Champlin "Charles Champlin") of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ wrote that the film made the transition from the stage "surprisingly well, given the odds," with "two of the most flamboyantly entertaining and skillful comedy performances of the year" by Jack Weston and Rita Moreno.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-30)

Moreno's appearance on _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_ earned her a [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Individual_Performance_in_a_Variety_or_Music_Program "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program") in 1977.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-31) As a result, she became the third person (after [Richard Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Rodgers "Richard Rodgers") and [Helen Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Hayes "Helen Hayes")) to have won an [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (1962), a [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy "Grammy") (1972), a [Tony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards "Tony Awards") (1975), and an [Emmy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy "Emmy") (1977), frequently referred to as an "[EGOT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EGOT "EGOT")". She won another Emmy award the following year, 1978, this time a [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actress_in_a_Drama_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series"), for her portrayal of former [call girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_girl "Call girl") Rita Kapcovic on a three-episode arc on _[The Rockford Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rockford\_Files "The Rockford Files")_.

In the 1980s, Moreno starred as Lucille in [Richard Benner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Benner "Richard Benner")'s comedy-drama film _[Happy Birthday, Gemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy\_Birthday,\_Gemini "Happy Birthday, Gemini")_ alongside [Madeline Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeline_Kahn "Madeline Kahn"). She was in [Alan Alda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Alda "Alan Alda")'s _[The Four Seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Seasons\_(1981\_film) "The Four Seasons (1981 film)")_ (1981) which was a financial and critical hit and starred Alda, [Carol Burnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Burnett "Carol Burnett"), [Len Cariou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Len_Cariou "Len Cariou"), [Sandy Dennis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandy_Dennis "Sandy Dennis"), and [Jack Weston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Weston "Jack Weston"). She was a regular on the three-season network run of _[9 to 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9\_to\_5\_(TV\_series) "9 to 5 (TV series)")_, a sitcom based on [the film hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9_to_5_(film) "9 to 5 (film)"), during the early 1980s.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-IMDb-32) Rita Moreno has made numerous guest appearances on television series in the 1980s, including _[The Love Boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Love\_Boat "The Love Boat")_, _[The Cosby Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cosby\_Show "The Cosby Show")_, _[The Golden Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Golden\_Girls "The Golden Girls")_, and _[Miami Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami\_Vice "Miami Vice")_. For her performance in _Two Ladies of Broadway_ (1992), Moreno drew inspiration from the "[Spanglish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanglish "Spanglish")" spoken by her mother, who visited the show in person.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera108-33)

In 1993, Moreno was invited to perform at President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton")'s inauguration and later that month was asked to perform at the White House.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-34) During the mid-1990s, Moreno provided the voice of [Carmen Sandiego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Sandiego_(character) "Carmen Sandiego (character)") on [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company")'s animated series _[Where on Earth Is Carmen Sandiego?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where\_on\_Earth\_Is\_Carmen\_Sandiego%3F "Where on Earth Is Carmen Sandiego?")_[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-35) In the franchise's [2019 animated series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Sandiego_(TV_series) "Carmen Sandiego (TV series)"), Moreno voices the character Cookie Booker. In the late 1990s, Moreno played [Sister Pete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_Pete "Sister Pete"), a nun trained as a psychologist in the popular [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") series _[Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_(TV\_series) "Oz (TV series)")_, for which she won several [ALMA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ALMA_Award "ALMA Award"). She made a guest appearance on _[The Nanny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Nanny "The Nanny")_ as Coach Stone, [Maggie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Sheffield "Margaret Sheffield")'s tyrannical gym teacher, whom [Fran Fine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran_Fine "Fran Fine") also remembered from her school as Ms. Wickavich.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-36)

### 2000s–2010s

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Rita_Moreno_2014.jpg/250px-Rita_Moreno_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rita_Moreno_2014.jpg)

Moreno in 2014

She released an eponymous album of nightclub songs in 2000 on the [Varèse Sarabande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Var%C3%A8se_Sarabande "Varèse Sarabande") label, with liner notes by [Michael Feinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Feinstein "Michael Feinstein").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-37) In 2006, she portrayed Amanda Wingfield in [Berkeley Repertory Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley_Repertory_Theatre "Berkeley Repertory Theatre")'s revival of _[The Glass Menagerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Glass\_Menagerie "The Glass Menagerie")_. She had a recurring role on _[Law & Order: Criminal Intent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law\_&\_Order:\_Criminal\_Intent "Law & Order: Criminal Intent")_ as the dying mother of Detective [Robert Goren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Goren "Robert Goren"). She played the family matriarch on the 2007 TV series _[Cane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cane\_(TV\_series) "Cane (TV series)")_, which starred [Jimmy Smits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Smits "Jimmy Smits") and [Hector Elizondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hector_Elizondo "Hector Elizondo"). She played the mother of [Fran Drescher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran_Drescher "Fran Drescher")'s character in the 2011–13 TV sitcom _[Happily Divorced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happily\_Divorced "Happily Divorced")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Since then, she has continued to work in film, including a small voice role in the 2014 film _[Rio 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio\_2 "Rio 2")_, perhaps her most commercially successful film. In September 2011, Moreno began performing a solo autobiographical show at the Berkeley Repertory Theatre, _Rita Moreno: Life Without Makeup_ written by the theatre's artistic director Tony Taccone after hours of interviews with Moreno.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-berkeleyside.com-21) In 2014, Moreno appeared in the NBC television film _Old Soul_, alongside [Natasha Lyonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natasha_Lyonne "Natasha Lyonne"), [Fred Willard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Willard "Fred Willard") and [Ellen Burstyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellen_Burstyn "Ellen Burstyn").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-38) The film was intended as a pilot for a television series, but it was not picked up.

Moreno plays the matriarch of a Cuban-American family in the Netflix sitcom _[One Day at a Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Day\_at\_a\_Time\_(2017\_TV\_series) "One Day at a Time (2017 TV series)")_, a remake produced by [Norman Lear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Lear "Norman Lear") of Lear's [1975–84 sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Day_at_a_Time_(1975_TV_series) "One Day at a Time (1975 TV series)"). The first season premiered in January 2017. Critics overall praised the show, and especially the performances of Moreno and the series' star, [Justina Machado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justina_Machado "Justina Machado").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-39) Also that year, Moreno and others contributed to [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda")'s single "[Almost Like Praying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almost_Like_Praying "Almost Like Praying")" where proceeds from the song went to the [Hispanic Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_Federation "Hispanic Federation")'s UNIDOS Disaster Relief program to benefit those affected by [Hurricane Maria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Maria "Hurricane Maria") that devastated the island of Puerto Rico.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-40)

### 2020s

In 2020–21, Moreno starred in and executive-produced the [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")–directed [adaptation of _West Side Story_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side_Story_(2021_film) "West Side Story (2021 film)").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-41) Moreno plays a newly created character, Valentina; she famously won the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") for playing Anita in [the 1961 original movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side_Story_(1961_film) "West Side Story (1961 film)"). The film was released on December 10, 2021. Justin Chang of _[NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR")_ wrote, "Sixty years later, Moreno is an executive producer on Spielberg's West Side Story. She also gives a poignant performance in the new role of Valentina, the widow of Doc, the drugstore owner. By her presence, Moreno teaches us how to approach this movie, as both an affectionate tribute and a gentle corrective."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-42)

Moreno played Angelica in _[Family Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family\_Switch "Family Switch")_.

## Personal life

From 1954 to 1962, Moreno was in an on-and-off relationship with [Marlon Brando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlon_Brando "Marlon Brando").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-46) She revealed in her memoir that she became pregnant by Brando and he arranged for an abortion. The abortion was botched, she went home and bled as the fetus died inside her and she had to be rushed to the hospital to have it surgically removed. Soon after, Brando fell in love with his co-star on _[Mutiny on the Bounty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutiny\_on\_the\_Bounty\_(1962\_film) "Mutiny on the Bounty (1962 film)")_[Tarita Teriipaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarita_Teri%CA%BBipaia "Tarita Teriʻipaia"), yet returned to her; Moreno attempted suicide by overdosing on Brando's sleeping pills.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-47) After the incident, Brando advised Moreno to go into therapy. They didn't reconnect until 1968 to film _[The Night of the Following Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Night\_of\_the\_Following\_Day "The Night of the Following Day")_. The two were on good terms after that and remained friends until Brando's death.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-48) Moreno also acknowledged that she dated [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley") "several times," though she described their romance as brief, claiming that she found Presley to be "sweet, but boring."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-49)

In 1965, Moreno married cardiologist and internist Leonard Gordon,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-legacy-latimes-50) who became her manager after he retired from medicine.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-51)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-datebook.sfchronicle.com-52) In 1995, they relocated to [Berkeley, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley,_California "Berkeley, California").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-SFGATE-2309622-53) They remained together until his death in 2010.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-54) Moreno and Gordon have one daughter, Fernanda Gordon Fisher, and two grandsons.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-55) Moreno said she once considered leaving her husband, but did not want to break up her family.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-beast-56)

## Acting credits and accolades

Bush stands with Rita Moreno](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/RitaMorenoPresidentialMedalofFreedom.jpg/250px-RitaMorenoPresidentialMedalofFreedom.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RitaMorenoPresidentialMedalofFreedom.jpg)

Moreno with President Bush in 2004, prior to receiving the Medal of Freedom

Main articles: [Rita Moreno on screen and stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno_on_screen_and_stage "Rita Moreno on screen and stage") and [List of awards and nominations received by Rita Moreno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Rita_Moreno "List of awards and nominations received by Rita Moreno")

Moreno has achieved what is called the [Triple Crown of Acting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_Crown_of_Acting "Triple Crown of Acting"), with individual competitive [Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"), [Emmy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy "Emmy") and [Tony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards "Tony Awards") awards for acting; as well as the [EGOT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EGOT "EGOT"). In 1962, she won the [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") for [Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") for _[West Side Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West\_Side\_Story\_(1961\_film) "West Side Story (1961 film)")_. When [Ariana DeBose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_DeBose "Ariana DeBose") won Best Supporting Actress for the same role in the [2021 adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side_Story_(2021_film) "West Side Story (2021 film)") of the film, Moreno and DeBose became the third pair of actors to win separate acting Oscars for portraying the same character. In 1972, she received a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") for [Best Children's Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Children's_Album "Grammy Award for Best Children's Album") for _[The Electric Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Electric\_Company "The Electric Company")_. In 1975, she won the [Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Play") for _[The Ritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ritz\_(play) "The Ritz (play)")_. She won her [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") in 1977 and 1978 for her performances in _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_ and _[The Rockford Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rockford\_Files "The Rockford Files")_, respectively.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-57)

She has also received a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award"), a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame"), she was Inducted into the [California Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Hall_of_Fame "California Hall of Fame"), 2007[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-58) When her star was unveiled, the celebration of "Rita Moreno Day" was also announced.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera141-7) The piece had been engraved in 1982 but remained in storage for a while.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera141-7) The celebration was in support of the Trust of the Latino Communities.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-Rivera141-7) In 2013, she received the [Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Life_Achievement_Award "Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award") which was presented to her by [Morgan Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Freeman "Morgan Freeman").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-59)

She has won numerous other honors, including various lifetime achievement awards and the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom"), America's highest civilian honor. In 2009, President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") presented her with the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-60) In 2015, she was awarded a [Kennedy Center Honors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center_Honors "Kennedy Center Honors") Lifetime Artistic Achievement Award for her contribution to American culture, through performing arts.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-61) She was awarded the [Peabody Career Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Award "Peabody Award") in 2019. She also received the [Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Life_Achievement_Award "Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award") in 2013, and was awarded the [Peabody Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Award "Peabody Award") in 2019.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-62) In October 2025, Moreno was honored with the [George Eastman Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Eastman_Award "George Eastman Award").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Moreno#cite_note-63)
